## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want tests that pin how scaled enemy counts reach the campaign (static and sequenced) without breaking determinism or the existing campaign invariants, so the density change cannot silently reshape the authored campaign.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Enemy counts rise with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Add tests (in the existing wave test files, or a new `src/waves/scaledCampaign.test.ts`) that:

- Assert level-1 `LEVELS` wave groups are unchanged by the scaling path (deep-equal counts), so onboarding data stays byte-identical.
- Assert a level-10 group grows by the documented multiplier with the documented rounding, floor of 1, 200-per-group cap, and `single`-formation groups remain exactly 1.
- Assert the scaling is applied to **both** the static `LEVELS` campaign and the sequenced campaign (`buildSequencedLevels`, covering `fixed`, `curve` and `dynamic` generation modes), through the shared build seam.
- Assert same-seed builds remain byte-identical (determinism contract) and that a second build of the same campaign is idempotent (no double scaling).
- Assert the scaled campaign still satisfies the existing invariants and wave-balance rules: `campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `campaignRoster.test.ts`, `waveBalance` R1–R3, `campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts`.
- Assert the shared helper is the only scaling implementation consumed by game and gym launch paths (parity seam), not a duplicated copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD for the specified reason (no scaling applied/nonexistent helper).
- Tests cover level-1 identity, level-10 growth, rounding, floor, cap, `single` groups, both campaign paths, same-seed determinism and no double scaling.
- Tests cover scaled-campaign compliance with the existing campaign invariants and wave-balance rules.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

**Key Files:**

- `src/waves/Formations.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- optionally `src/waves/scaledCampaign.test.ts` (new)
- existing invariant suites: `src/waves/campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `src/core/waveBalance.test.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Add level-scaling module and tunable rules" (needs the helper contract). Blocks the campaign count-application feature.

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want deterministic tests that prove the kill-time power-up supply falls with the campaign level, so the supply curve cannot regress unnoticed.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Power-up supply per enemy falls with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Extend `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (and the rules tests where appropriate) with tests that:

- Force the scene RNG so the number of drops over N kills is exact and deterministic at level 1 (matches the current 0.18 rate) and at level 10 (matches 0.05, i.e. at most 30 % of the level-1 rate).
- Prove the level is resolved from the live campaign (`WaveManager.currentLevel()?.level`), i.e. after advancing a level the next kills use the new chance, and an unknown level falls back to level 1.
- Prove the small-asteroid Extra Life roll scales by the same ratio and is unchanged at level 1 (`rules.asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`).
- Prove drop types/weights, the mineral kill-drop rule and timed weapon/power-up effects are unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD (flat 0.18 roll for every level).
- Assertions are exact and seeded — no statistical/threshold flakiness.
- Coverage includes level 1 identity, level 10 endpoint, mid-run level advance, unknown-level fallback and Extra Life proportionality.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- `src/core/rules.test.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Add level-scaling module and tunable rules". Blocks the PlayScene drop-roll feature.

## Goal (tracer-bullet vertical slice)

Ship the first end-to-end music slice: the menu/attract ambient track ("Star Drift", Lydian) played through the existing shared AudioContext, driven by a minimal music state machine, with the autoplay/gesture guard and an independent music volume control.

This slice cuts through every layer — baked asset, playback facade, state machine, scene wiring, settings, tests, docs — so later slices extend a proven path rather than a horizontal layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The menu/attract state plays the baked "Star Drift" Lydian ambient stem as a seamless loop.
- [ ] Music starts only after a user gesture, honouring the AudioContext resume discipline (GDD 7.3), and reuses the single shared AudioContext owned by the playback provider.
- [ ] Music volume and mute are independent of SFX and persisted in the settings record.
- [ ] The state machine enters and leaves the menu/attract state only at a bar boundary of the shared beat clock.
- [ ] Unit tests cover stem looping, the gesture guard, independent volume routing and the menu/attract transition; all playback degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext.

- [ ] Covers parent AC5: **Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.

## Minimal implementation

1. Bake the "Star Drift" ambient stem via the ToneForge pipeline and add it to the cue/stem manifest (smallest slice of the stem pipeline).
2. Add src/audio/music/musicPlayer.ts (facade) and a minimal src/audio/music/musicStateMachine.ts with the menu/attract state.
3. Wire gesture-driven start/resume through MenuScene using the shared AudioContext.
4. Extend SettingsRecord with musicVolume/musicMuted and route them independently of SFX.
5. Add unit tests for each acceptance criterion.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by Music contract mapping and traceability guard (AH-0MVMH2OPY001X6M3), which is itself blocked by the chapter docs item (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W).
- Reuses the shared AudioContext and provider seam in src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts.

## Risky assumption

Baked stems (not runtime synthesis) are the delivery mechanism, consistent with the shipped ToneForge pipeline; recorded as an assumption in the parent item's plan.

**Key Files:**
- src/audio/music/musicPlayer.ts (new)
- src/audio/music/musicStateMachine.ts (new)

# Win path: suppress the mini-boss wheel and bank a fixed post-win bonus on hex wins (AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2)

Discovered-from: AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA (Re-baseline salvage, cores and the mini-boss reward value per hex deployment).

## Problem statement

With a hex deployment ending on its level's wave-10 mini-boss (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2), a winning deployment presents the mini-boss wheel reward **after** the run has finished (Q2 = b ordering: defeat → defence report → reward → map). The wheel's run-scoped permanent upgrades are applied to a completed run and have no further effect, so the post-win reveal reads as a broken reward. The producer's ruling on the OPEN QUESTION (recorded on AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA, 2026-11-13) is **Q1 = (c)**: suppress the wheel on the win path and bank a **fixed post-win bonus** into the hangar war instead.

## Users

- **As a Hangar War player**, after I win a hex deployment I want the post-win moment to pay into my persistent war (a banked bonus), not a wheel whose upgrades vanish into the finished run, so the reward reads as real progress.
- **As a producer**, I want the decision implemented exactly: arcade and loss paths keep the wheel as shipped; only the winning hangar deployment path changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Whole win-path reward surface suppressed on the winning hangar deployment path.** A winning hex deployment presents **no reward overlay** on the win path — neither `MiniBossWheelScene` nor the empty-owned three-option choice fallback (`pendingWinReward` is not carried); the player still sees the mini-boss defeat, then `DefenceReportScene` (which now announces the banked win bonus, Q3 = b), then the map. The bonus is banked as part of the win resolution. Pinned by a scene test through the shipped win-path wiring.
2. **Fixed post-win bonus banked — minerals, baselined from measurement.** The win resolution banks the fixed bonus as **minerals only** (Q2 = a) through the pure hangarWar banking/economy seams (`salvageBanking.ts` / `hangarEconomy.ts`), not a forked write. The amount is **baselined from AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA's measured per-deployment income** (Q1 = b; `wl dep` dependency on that item) and is stated as a named constant when set; this item does not invent the number. The banked balance is persisted through the one `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload write.
3. **Other paths unchanged.** The arcade campaign still shows the wheel on every mini-boss defeat, and a lost hangar deployment still shows no wheel and no bonus (report → map). Existing campaign/mini-boss suites pass without behavioural edits.
4. **Docs.** The GDD §8.2 win-path sentence (the "mini-boss **reward** overlay" / win-path reward line) and any affected code comments state the suppression + fixed mineral bonus on the winning hangar deployment path, the report announcement (Q3 = b), and the recorded decisions (Q1 = c, Q2 = a, Q3 = b; AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA), including any relevant wiki/docs-site entries.
5. **Full project test suite** passes with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who wins a hex deployment now sees their win bank real, persistent minerals into the hangar war — announced on the defence report instead of a wheel that spent its upgrades on an already-finished run.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — the hangar-deployment win-path transition (`_finaliseHangarWarMiniBossVictory` / `_resolveHangarWarWinReward` / `_resolveHangarWarCapture`); suppress the wheel and bank the bonus.
- `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts` — the win-path reward presentation seam; replace the wheel reveal with the banked-bonus announcement (Q3 = b).
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` / `MineralChoiceScene` — unchanged surfaces (still the arcade/gym rewards); the win path simply no longer launches them.
- `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — the pure banking/economy seams the bonus writes through.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — the payload fields (`bankedMinerals` / `bankedCores`) the bonus lands in.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.captureCycle.test.ts`, `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.hexMiniBossVictory.test.ts` — the seams to pin.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 — the win-path economy notes to update.

## Constraints and assumptions

- **Bonus amount baselined from measurement (Q1 = b).** The amount is derived from AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA's measured per-deployment income once that lands; this item has a `wl dep` dependency on it for the number, and the number is recorded on the item (as a named constant) when set. No invented number here.
- **Minerals only (Q2 = a).** The bonus banks minerals; cores are not granted by the win-path bonus (a captured deployment already banks its one core via the capture cycle — adding bonus cores would double-count).
- **Win path only.** Suppression is scoped to winning hangar deployments; nothing else moves (gym↔game parity for the shared wheel surface stays intact — the wheel remains the arcade/gym reward).
- **Pure seams.** All bonus banking resolves in `src/core/hangarWar/`; scenes only wire it.
- **Announced, not silently banked (Q3 = b).** `DefenceReportScene` announces the banked bonus before the map so the win "reads as real progress".
- **"The wheel" = the whole win-path reward surface.** The recorded decision suppresses the win-path *reward overlay* — the wheel and the empty-owned fallback choice alike, since both grant run-scoped value to a finished run (recorded interpretation of Q1 = c, 2026-11-13).
- **Scope-creep guard.** A change to banking rules, prices, the bonus amount's balance, unlock pacing, or the measured income itself is a further linked item, not folded in here.

## Existing state (researched, with evidence)

- **Win path wiring exists.** `PlayScene._finaliseHangarWarMiniBossVictory` resolves capture, resolves the win reward (`_resolveHangarWarWinReward` → `drawWheelOutcome`/`buildWheelWedges`/`applyWheelOutcome`, or the empty-owned three-option choice), stores `pendingWinReward`, then transitions via `DefenceReportScene`, which launches the wheel overlay (`_presentReward`), then the map. The wheel's `applyWheelOutcome` grants run-scoped permanent levels to the finished run (`src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts:348`).
- **Pure banking seams.** `bankSalvage` (salvageBanking.ts) copies cumulative minerals + cores with a per-run watermark; `resolveHexCapture` (captureCycle.ts) banks the run's salvage and marks the hex; `hangarEconomy.ts` holds `CORE_MINERAL_EQUIVALENT = 100` and the pricing/purchase rules; the balance persists via `hangarWarStore` in the `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload.
- **The GDD §8.2 win-path sentence** currently reads "…the mini-boss **reward** overlay (the same shared `MiniBossWheelScene` the arcade uses) …" — this is the sentence AC4 updates.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: the measurement dependency is still open.** The bonus amount waits on AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA's measured per-deployment income (Q1 = b); until it lands, the named constant is provisional and AC2's amount assertion is pinned once set. The banking/wiring change does not depend on the number (only the value does).
- **Assumption: suppression covers the empty-owned fallback too.** The recorded decision (Q1 = c) is read as removing the *whole* win-path reward overlay, not just `MiniBossWheelScene`; an empty-owned win must not present the three-option choice either (it also grants run-scoped value). If the producer intended the fallback to survive, AC1 narrows accordingly.
- **Scope-creep risk:** re-tuning the bonus amount, banking rules, prices or unlock pacing is a further linked item, never folded in here.

## Related work

- **Re-baseline salvage, cores and the mini-boss reward value per hex deployment (AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA)** — records the producer decision this implements (Q1 = c) and is the source of the measured per-deployment income the bonus amount is baselined from (blocking `wl dep` dependency).
- **In HexMap killing the mini-boss wins the hex (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2)** — the parent change that introduced the post-win reward positioning.
- **Win-path reward after the defence report (AH-0MWCOW6KA008OJOL)** — the change that introduced the win-path reward ordering this item suppresses/replaces (completed).
- Repository references: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 / §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md`, `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/{salvageBanking,hangarEconomy,captureCycle}.ts`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWCOW6KA008OJOL** – Win-path reward after the defence report (completed)
- **AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA** – Re-baseline salvage, cores and the mini-boss reward value per hex deployment (open)
- **AH-0MWCOW4IQ003XST5** – Mini-boss victory captures the hex and ends the run (completed)

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What is the fixed post-win bonus amount, and what rules the knob?**
  - Asked: 2026-11-13 (intake, producer-review round 1). Answered 2026-11-13 (producer, interactive reply).
  - Question: The recorded decision (Q1 = c on AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA) suppresses the wheel on the win path and banks a fixed post-win bonus, with the amount a balance knob either producer-specified or baselined from that item's measured per-deployment income.
  - Options: (a) producer-specified now; (b) baselined from AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA's measured income once it lands (blocks this item on the dependency); (c) freeform.
  - **Recommended: (a).** — a concrete number now makes AC2 fully testable immediately without waiting on the open measurement item.
  - **Answer (producer): (b)** — the amount is baselined from AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA's measured per-deployment income once it lands; recorded as a named constant, `wl dep` dependency on that item.
  - Status: **ANSWERED** (recorded in AC2 / Constraints).
- **Q2 — What does the fixed bonus pay out in?**
  - Asked: 2026-11-13 (intake, producer-review round 1). Answered 2026-11-13 (producer, interactive reply).
  - Options: (a) minerals only; (b) cores only; (c) fixed package.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — cores are the scarcer currency and already bank one per capture; a mineral grant reads naturally.
  - **Answer (producer): (a) minerals only.**
  - Status: **ANSWERED** (recorded in AC2 / Constraints).
- **Q3 — Does the player see the banked bonus on the win path?**
  - Asked: 2026-11-13 (intake, producer-review round 1). Answered 2026-11-13 (producer, interactive reply).
  - Options: (a) silently banked; (b) announced in `DefenceReportScene` ('win bonus banked: +N' before the map); (c) freeform.
  - **Recommended: (b)** — the user story requires the post-win reward to "read as real progress".
  - **Answer (producer): (b)** — announced in `DefenceReportScene` before the map.
  - Status: **ANSWERED** (recorded in AC1 / AC4 / Constraints).

# Rebalance ring 1's grind budget: measured 16.4 min against the authored 40–60 min window

Discovered-from: AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V (Budget verdicts and linked rebalancing
items), part of the re-measurement chain under AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A (Re-measure
ring timing for one-level hex deployments). **Producer ruling required** — this
item records the evidence and the options; it does not decide which way the
budget should move.

## Why this item exists

`RING_TIMING_TARGETS` authors ring 1's grind window as **40–60 minutes** with a
±10 % tolerance of the window's width (**±2 minutes**), judged on the **grind**
line. The regenerated artifact (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, produced
by `AH-0MWCQ4GTE005YG02` from the shipped code) measures the shipped one-level
five-wave sortie at **16.4 minutes**, so the authored window no longer holds.
The parent's acceptance criteria forbid silently re-wording a missed budget,
so the miss is recorded here and the ruling is left to the producer.

## Measurement (source: `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, ring 1, `grind`, seeds 1–3)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verdict | **missed** (`withinWindow: false`, `withinTolerance: false`) |
| Measured total mean | **16.4256 min** (seeds: 15.7239 / 16.6383 / 16.9144) |
| Measured total min–max | **15.7239 – 16.9144 min** |
| Authored window | **40 – 60 min** |
| Tolerance | ±10 % of window width = **±2 min** (tolerance floor 38 min) |
| Delta to window floor | **−23.5744 min** below 40 min; **−21.5744 min** below the 38 min tolerance floor |
| Deployment minutes (measured, mean) | 2.2128 (1.8619 / 2.3192 / 2.4572) |
| Between-sortie minutes (modelled) | 12.0 (2 min × 6 hexes) |
| Retry minutes (measured replay) | 2.2128 (= the replayed deployment's measured length) |
| Re-capture minutes (modelled) | 0.0 (the grind line secures the ring) |
| Split check | 2.2128 + 12.0 + 2.2128 + 0.0 = 16.4256 = the total mean |
| Captured / lost sorties | 0.0 / **6.0** per run — every sortie is a first-attempt loss to enemy fire and is retried |
| Ring secured | 3 / 3 runs (the grind plays every hex, so the ring still ends secured) |
| Salvage | 0.0 banked, 15.0 forfeited (mean: 25 / 4 / 16) |

## Before/after attributable to the one-level model

| Ring 1 grind | Before (campaign slice) | After (one-level sortie) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total mean (min–max) | 54.3 (51.0–56.6) | **16.4 (15.7–16.9)** | −37.9 min |
| Verdict | in-window (40–60) | **missed (40–60)** | window no longer holds |
| Deployment minutes | 19.0 | 2.2 | −16.8 (the slice no longer climbs campaign levels past the hex's own) |
| Retry minutes | 23.3 | 2.2 | −21.1 (retry now charges the replayed deployment's measured length, not a flat 5 min) |
| Between-sortie minutes | 12.0 | 12.0 | unchanged (2 min × 6 hexes) |
| Re-capture minutes | 0.0 | 0.0 | unchanged on the grind line |
| Captured / lost | 1.3 / 4.7 | 0.0 / 6.0 | no sortie clears under the per-level arena's fire-on fidelity |
| Salvage banked / forfeited | 24.0 / 54.0 | 0.0 / 15.0 | no capture ⇒ no banking |

The dominant driver is the deployment model itself: a deployment's measured
arena time fell from ≈3.2 min to ≈0.4 min, and the retry term follows it
mechanically (retry = the replayed deployment's measured length). The
between-sortie allowance (2 min) and the re-capture allowance are unchanged and
do not drive the delta.

## Options (for the producer; not a recommendation)

1. **Re-author the ring-1 window** (e.g. from 40–60 min to a window the shipped
   one-level model measures). Cheapest, but it changes the design of record
   (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Session shape) rather than the game.
2. **Tune the authored ring data** — more hexes in ring 1, or higher
   aggression/level per hex — so a ring-1 clear takes the authored time. This
   changes gameplay pace, not the timing model.
3. **Revisit the allowances** — the between-sortie 2 minutes, the retry rule
   (one modelled replay per loss) and the rush re-capture charge. A larger
   between-sortie or retry allowance would lengthen the measured total, but it
   prices a deployment time the harness does not measure.
4. **Revisit the measurement boundary** — the per-level arena ignores the wave
   `shootEnabled` gate, so every sortie is lost to enemy fire and none is
   captured. Honouring the gate (or modelling the mini-boss encounter, also
   unmodelled) would raise captures and change the measured total; that is a
   harness/model decision (`AH-0MWCQ4FWN009J9DM` chain), not a budget re-word.

## Acceptance criteria

- The producer rules on one of the options (or another) and records the
  decision on this item; **no option is taken implicitly** by a later code or
  docs change.
- If the ruling re-authors the window, `RING_TIMING_TARGETS`, the docs guards
  (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`, `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`) and
  the quoted documents are updated together and the artifact re-judged.
- If the ruling tunes the ring data or the allowances, the artifact is
  regenerated with the documented command and the before/after evidence is
  recorded here.
- Whatever the ruling, ring 1's grind verdict is stated honestly (measured
  figure, window, delta) — never re-worded as passing.
- The full project test suite passes with the change.

**Related:** `related-to:AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A`,
`discovered-from:AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V`,
`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`
(`RING_TIMING_TARGETS`), `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Session shape.

- `README.md` — matched: 0mwcowsvn003x81a, 0mwcq4htc004u73v, acceptance, aggression, also (+171 more)

Parent: AH-0MWCB6021008L4YN (Ring-timing text report prints seed 1's retry, between-sortie and re-capture minutes as if they were the multi-seed figures).

## Goal (user story)

As a ring-timing harness operator, I want every metric line of `formatRingTimingReport` to describe the seed set (not seed 1's sample), so the text report and the JSON artefact agree.

## Summary

`formatRingTimingReport` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) renders `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` from `report.runs[0]` (seed 1) while every other line uses the summary means. Add the missing aggregate stats to `RingTimingSummary`, render from the summary, and regenerate the committed artefact so its JSON summary carries the new fields.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `RingTimingSummary` gains `betweenSortieMinutes`, `retryMinutes`, `retakeMinutes` and `expectedRetakes` as `RingTimingStats` (count/mean/min/max), populated in `simulateRingTiming` via `stats(runs.map(...))`.
- `formatRingTimingReport` renders `between sorties`, `retries` and `exposed re-capture` from the summary aggregates (mean, with min-max where the JSON summary carries them) - never from `report.runs[0]`; a single-seed report still renders that seed's figures under its `seed 1` header.
- `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` is regenerated (`npm run ring-timing -- --json --out docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, default rings/lines/seeds 1-3): deterministic, so every existing mean/min/max value is unchanged and the summary merely gains the four new fields; the committed-evidence tests still pass.
- The sibling pinning test (AH-0MWGVXB95002W7KI) passes; the full project test suite passes via the test skill at the dev-push gate.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend the `RingTimingSummary` interface and its construction in `simulateRingTiming`.
- Update the three lines of `formatRingTimingReport` to read `summary.*.mean` (min-max where carried), mirroring the `total` line's style.
- Regenerate the committed artefact via the CLI; update the fixture type `CommittedBaselineReport` only if its partial shape needs extending (it already tolerates extra keys).
- Verify via `/skill:test` (never ad-hoc test commands): changed-scope gate, then the committed-evidence suite / full gate.

## Constraints

- Reporting/consistency fix only: no behaviour or measured-value changes; the regenerated artefact's existing totals must be byte-identical in value.
- Additive JSON arity: no exported `RingTimingSummary` field is renamed or removed.
- UK English.

## Risky assumptions

- Regeneration is deterministic (asserted by the existing determinism test): same seeds/options reproduce identical values, so committed totals cannot drift. Success threshold: the regenerated artefact's existing mean/min/max are unchanged.

## Goal (user story)

As a reader of `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline*, I want the quoted retry minutes and share to come from the multi-seed aggregate, consistent with the rendered report and the committed artefact.

## Summary

The old baseline quote paired seed 1's retry total with the mean total ("55 of its 116.4 min"). After the regenerated baseline, quote the retry minutes and share from the aggregate for the grind line, matching the rendered report and the regenerated `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/EVALUATION.md` § *Measured baseline* quotes the retry minutes and share from the aggregate, consistent with the rendered report and the committed artefact; no line silently reports seed 1 as the seed-set figure.
- The quoted figure equals the mean of the committed per-seed `retryMinutes` (e.g. ring 2 grind: retries ≈12.0 min of the ≈48.1 min mean total, ≈25 % share) and matches the rendered report's retries line.
- No seed-1-only figure appears as a seed-set figure anywhere in `docs/EVALUATION.md` (grep-check the retry/re-capture mentions).
- The budget verdicts and their rebalancing-item links are unchanged (still `missed`, AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X / AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5).

## Minimal implementation

- Read the aggregate retry figures from the regenerated artefact (the implement sibling's new summary fields / per-run means).
- Amend the retry-allowance sentence in § *Measured baseline* to quote the aggregate retry minutes and its share of the mean total, in the style of the older quote but aggregate-consistent.
- Cross-check the figures against the rendered report text and commit the docs change with the parent work-item reference.

## Constraints

- Numbers come from the committed artefact, never hand-edited; UK English.

## Problem statement

In Hex War (the Hangar War ring) a between-sortie frontier tick can launch an attack **from** the very hex the player's current sortie is attacking. A hex that is fighting off the player — "too busy defending" — should not simultaneously press an attack on a neighbouring player-held hex.

## Users

- **Hangar War player (mid-ring).** "I deploy at hex X to take it. On landing I find X also hit one of my held hexes during the tick — it was supposed to be defending against me, not attacking me." The player experiences a defence that cannot be answered: the origin hex is the hex they just fought.
- **Product/design owner.** Wants the rule "an attacked hex defends, it does not attack" so committing to a sortie has a legible, fair consequence instead of a free counter-punch.

Example user stories:

1. As a player attacking hex *X*, I want *X* to be unable to launch an attack this tick, so that my defence push cannot be punished by the hex I am pushing.
2. As a player attacking hex *X* whose neighbouring held hex is also reachable from unheld hex *Y*, I still expect pressure from *Y*, so the ring keeps squeezing me even while I commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A between-sortie tick resolved for a hex the player is attacking never records that hex as an attack origin: every entry in the tick record's `attacks` names a different unheld neighbour, and a held target whose **only** unheld neighbour is the attacked hex draws no attack at all (no record entry, no throw).
- When another unheld neighbour of the target exists, the attack still happens from the neighbour the existing selection order names next (most aggressive, ties settled by sorted id), so the rule suppresses only the origin, not the attack: the recorded force, aggression multiplier, jitter, attack strength and margin are the ones that neighbour produces.
- A tick resolved without a player-attacking hex (the arcade run, a deployment whose `hexId` is `null`, a hex id absent from the ring) is byte-identical to today's behaviour: the existing `resolveDefence`, `attackingNeighbour` and `runFrontierTick` tests, and the queued-attack (pending) cases, pass unchanged.
- `PlayScene` passes the current deployment's target hex on **both** tick paths — the winning path (tick resolved at mini-boss defeat, before the capture) and the losing path (tick resolved at run end) — and replay determinism holds: the same payload, seed, tick and attacking hex produce an identical payload and record, and a different attacking hex deterministically changes only the origins it excludes.
- `GymHexWar` can declare the hex the player is attacking and both its control-surface tick and its rendered attack arrows honour the rule through the shipped code path (no gym-local copy of the rule), with `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` recording the surface.
- Automated tests pin: origin exclusion (frontier draw and queued attack), fallback origin, the no-exclusion regression, both `PlayScene` tick paths and the gym surface.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A hex you are attacking now defends instead of striking back, so committing to a sortie can no longer hand a neighbouring enemy hex a free hit on your held hexes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** The rule lives once, in the shared pure frontier tick (`src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`), and is consumed by the game (`PlayScene`) and the gym (`GymHexWar`). The gym may not carry its own copy; a divergent harness double must record the reason in the work item and in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
- **Purity and determinism.** The tick stays pure (the caller's payload is never mutated) and replayable from `(seed, tick)`. The exclusion must be derived from parameters, never from wall clock or scene state read inside the resolver, and must never consume or reorder the seeded draws in a way that breaks the "same payload ⇒ same record" property for an unchanged attacking hex.
- **No new persisted payload fields.** The attacking hex is the deployment's existing `hexId` (`HangarWarDeployment.hexId`), so nothing is added to `HangarWarPayload` and the store's field-presence migration pattern is untouched.
- **No simulated battle.** The defence stays an arithmetic comparison over stored numbers; this rule only restricts *who may launch*, never adds a battle loop.
- **Scope discipline.** Not in scope: re-balancing aggression, changing the 70 % attack chance, changing which held hex the frontier targets beyond the necessary "this target lost its only origin", or any live hex-vs-hex combat (there is none — Hex War is an algorithmic between-sortie loop).

## Existing state

- `runFrontierTick` (`src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`) runs one between-sortie tick: it redistributes aggression, resolves queued `pendingAttacks` first, then (only when nothing was queued and the seeded draw passes the 70 % attack chance) attacks **one** held, attackable hex.
- The attack origin is always derived by `attackingNeighbour(hex, hexes)` — the **most aggressive unheld neighbouring hex of the same ring**, ties settled by sorted id. `resolveAttack` uses that origin for the force (`baseAttackingForce + origin aggression × forcePerOriginAggression`) and for the attacker type (the origin's authored boss).
- `PlayScene._resolveBetweenSortieTick()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`) resolves the tick from `frontierClockFor(payload)` and persists the result. It is called on the winning path from `_finaliseHangarWarMiniBossVictory` (before `_resolveHangarWarCapture`, deliberately, so the newly won hex cannot be attacked by the same tick) and on the losing path from the run-end handoff to `HexMapScene`. Neither path tells the tick which hex the player attacked, even though `this.hangarWarDeployment.hexId` holds exactly that.
- The tick's record is what the map renders (attack arrows plus the left-hand attack panel via `buildHexMapModel` / `renderHexMap`); `GymHexWar` renders the same shipped record and drives its `take hex → leave bot → tick` surface through the harness double `applyFakeFrontierTick` (`src/core/hangarWar/fakeFrontierClock.ts`).
- Because the winning tick resolves *before* the capture, the attacked hex is still **unheld** at tick time — i.e. exactly the kind of hex that qualifies as an attack origin today, so the reported behaviour is reproducible.

## Desired change

A new, optional input to the frontier tick: **the hex the player is currently attacking** (the deployment's target). While supplied, that hex is excluded from origin selection:

1. `attackingNeighbour` gains an optional exclusion (the attacked hex id, or a set of excluded ids) and returns the best remaining unheld neighbour, or `null` when the attacked hex was the only one.
2. `runFrontierTick` threads that exclusion through **both** launch paths — the queued (`pendingAttacks`) resolution and the frontier draw — and through the "is this hex attackable" filter used to choose the frontier's target, so a target that lost its only origin simply is not attacked this tick (the frontier may then attack a different eligible held hex, exactly as it does today when no target is attackable).
3. `FrontierTickOptions` gains a documented optional field (naming suggestion: `playerAttackingHexId?: string | null`) defaulting to `null` = today's behaviour; the record gains no new fields, because a suppressed origin produces no attack entry at all.
4. `PlayScene._resolveBetweenSortieTick()` passes `this.hangarWarDeployment?.hexId ?? null`.
5. `GymHexWar` gains a control-surface setter for the hex the player is attacking (e.g. `attackHex(hexId)` / `setPlayerAttackingHex(hexId)`), passes it to its shipped `runFrontierTick` record, and the harness double `applyFakeFrontierTick` honours the same exclusion so the gym's `tick()` surface stays consistent with the game rule.

## Key Files

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — add the optional exclusion to `attackingNeighbour`, thread it through `resolveAttack` / `runFrontierTick` (queued and frontier paths) and document the rule in the module header ("Who attacks, and where from").
- `src/core/hangarWar/fakeFrontierClock.ts` — mirror the exclusion in the harness tick double so the gym's control-surface tick matches the shipped rule.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_resolveBetweenSortieTick()` passes the deployment's target hex (covers both the winning and losing call sites; the doc comment on `pendingBetweenSortieTick` needs the new rationale).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — control-surface setter for the attacked hex, threaded into `shippedTickRecord()` and the harness tick; add it to the gym's documented control surface.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.test.ts` — origin exclusion, fallback origin, quiet-tick and no-exclusion regression cases.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.captureCycle.test.ts` — both tick paths pass the deployment's target hex and the recorded origins never name it.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts` — the gym's attacked-hex surface and its rendered record.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.2's between-sortie tick description (the "An attack is always launched from an unheld neighbouring hex" paragraph).
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — `GymHexWar` row: the attacked-hex control surface and its parity status.

## Related work

- `AH-0MVUXCA0J0011W88` — Pure defence resolver and frontier aggression clock (the tick and `attackingNeighbour` this changes).
- `AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP` — the between-sortie tick wired into `PlayScene`; the win-path ordering ("tick before capture") is its deliberate rule and stays.
- `AH-0MWEXI5460080WEI`, `AH-0MWEXIAEQ004IT0R`, `AH-0MWEXIHHK007H32A` — attack arrows and the left-hand attack panel that render this record.
- `AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP` — defence report rolled into the hex map (no report screen).
- `AH-0MVUXC94N008MV63`, `AH-0MWEZZDJC009FEU7` — `GymHexWar` harness and the ring-end assault surface.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 — design of record for the frontier clock and the answerability rule.
- `AH-0MWEW5QCR009NX0V`, `AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG` — the hex-variety pass that recently touched the same map/tick surfaces.

## Assumptions and open questions

Applied assumptions (recommended interpretations, recorded for producer review — see the work item's comment and the Appendix):

- **A1 — Which hex.** "The hex the player is attacking" is the current deployment's target (`HangarWarDeployment.hexId`), and the rule applies to the single between-sortie tick resolved for that sortie. Hex War has no live hex-vs-hex combat for the rule to run in.
- **A2 — Both sortie endings.** The rule applies to a winning sortie (tick resolved at mini-boss defeat, before the capture) and to a losing sortie (tick resolved at run end), because the player was attacking that hex in both cases.
- **A3 — Suppress the origin, not the attack.** If another unheld neighbour exists the attack still rides from it; if none exists the target is simply not attacked this tick, consistent with the existing "unanswerable attacks are dropped" rule.
- **A4 — Queued attacks are dropped, not retried.** A `pendingAttacks` entry whose only origin is the attacked hex is consumed and dropped this tick, exactly like today's stale/unanswerable queue entries, so the queue can still never deadlock.
- **A5 — No persistence.** The exclusion is a per-tick argument; nothing is stored on the payload and no save migration is involved.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- Q: "Should the rule also apply to the tick resolved at the end of a **losing** sortie, or only a winning one?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer answer available in this session. Assumption applied (recommended option): yes, both endings, because the player was attacking that hex up to the tick. Source: pending producer confirmation; ticket comment records the question.
- Q: "A queued (`pendingAttacks`) attack whose only possible origin is the attacked hex: drop it this tick, or keep it queued?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — assumption applied (recommended option): drop it, matching the shipped rule that unanswerable queue entries are consumed and never retried. Source: pending producer confirmation.
- Q: "Does the exclusion outlive the sortie (e.g. the hex stays unable to attack until the player's attack is 'spent')?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — assumption applied (recommended option): no, it applies to that sortie's single tick only; afterwards the hex behaves as today. Source: pending producer confirmation.
- Q: "Is Hex War a live battle in which a defending hex currently fires back?" — Answer: no — research: `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`_resolveBetweenSortieTick`) and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 show the frontier is an algorithmic between-sortie resolution over stored numbers, with exactly one tick per deployment. Source: repository inspection.
- Q: "Does the attacked hex currently qualify as an attack origin?" — Answer: yes — research: the winning tick resolves *before* the capture, so the attacked hex is still unheld and `attackingNeighbour` may select it (most aggressive neighbour wins). Source: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:3864`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` (`attackingNeighbour`, `resolveAttack`).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXCA0J0011W88** – Pure defence resolver and frontier aggression clock (completed)
- **AH-0MWEXI5460080WEI** – Tests: attack arrows + left-hand attack panel (model + renderer) (completed)
- **AH-0MWEXIHHK007H32A** – Renderer: draw attack arrows and the left-hand attack-details panel on the hex map (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvwzyqn8007sxig, absent, acceptance, add, added (+383 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvwzyqn8007sxig, absent, acceptance, add, added (+365 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, add, added, adds (+319 more)

# Strengthen a hexes defence

Problem statement: A player who owns a hex has no way to spend their banked salvage to make the bot defending it stronger. This item adds an "Upgrade Defences" flow: select a held hex on the map, open a hangar-style upgrade screen targeting that hex's bot, and spend minerals/cores on hangar-catalogue upgrades that fit the bot's ship.

## Users (with user stories)

- **Player (primary).** "When I select a hex I own, I want to send upgrades to the bot defending it, so the salvage I earned strengthens a hold I care about."
- **Player, making a purchase.** "I want to buy upgrades with minerals and/or cores from the Hangar, and only those that fit into the bot's existing ship — an upgrade to a weapon it already carries, or a new weapon in an empty slot."
- **Player, after a tick.** "I want the upgrades to stay on the bot between sorties, and to be gone for good if the hex loses its defence, so spending salvage is a real commitment."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Selecting a **held** hex on the hex map surfaces an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action; activating it opens the bot-upgrade screen for that hex's defender. An unheld hex offers no such action, and the read-only `GymHexWar` map render never offers it either.
- The bot-upgrade screen reuses the shared hangar-screen model/renderer pattern (game and `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` parity): it lists the hangar-catalogue entries (weapons, hulls and modifiers) and shows each one's fit verdict for the focused bot — **upgrade existing** (the bot already carries the weapon → raise its level), **add to empty slot** (a weapon kind the bot does not carry → offered **only** when the bot has a free permanent slot), **re-hull** (a hull entry), **train** (a modifier entry), or a disabled reason (slot pool full / unaffordable / ring-gated). No second, drifting copy of the fit rule exists.
- A purchase is paid for in minerals and/or cores from the fleet's banked salvage (the hangar wallet, `HangarState.bankedMinerals`/`bankedCores`), spends exactly the displayed price, and applies the upgrade to the bot's ship: a new weapon kind occupies one permanent slot at level 1, an already-carried weapon rises one level, a hull entry swaps the bot's `hullId` (keeping the existing carried loadout), and a modifier entry applies its effect to the bot. The fleet's owned sets, active hull/loadout and the player's deployed ship are untouched by a bot purchase.
- Weapon upgrades follow a **per-level upgrade price** (Q9 = B): a separate, authored upgrade-price rule for raising an already-carried weapon's level, distinct from the catalogue entry's purchase price for a new kind; both are documented in one pricing table.
- The bot's defence rating reflects the sent upgrades through the **one** existing rating formula (`defenderRatingFromSnapshot` / the `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS` mapping); a purchase returns a fresh payload with the defender's stored `defenceRating` recomputed and re-persisted, never a second derivation.
- Upgrade state persists on the `HexDefender` across between-sortie ticks and save/load round-trips (additive optional fields, field-presence migration, same pattern as `skills`), and is destroyed with the bot when its hex falls in a defence tick (existing `applyDefence` path — a fallen hex loses its defender).
- Tests cover: the fit rule (upgrade-existing vs add-to-empty-slot vs re-hull vs train vs disabled states), purchase economics (price, per-level upgrade price, wallet deduction, refused purchases), snapshot update + rating recompute, persistence round-trip and fall-destruction, corruption tolerance of the stored upgrade state, the map action surface and the gym parity assertion.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` for the new bot-upgrade control surface.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player can now spend earned minerals and cores to send hangar upgrades — weapons, hulls and modifiers — to a bot defending a hex they own, and read the strengthened rating on the map; giving the hangar economy a second, defence-shaped sink.

## Constraints

- **Pure and injectable:** the fit rule, purchase application and rating recompute live in the pure core (hangar economy / a new `botUpgrade` module), no Phaser, no storage access; scenes only present and persist.
- **Same-data-model rule (producer Q2):** the bot uses the same ship data model as a player-controlled ship — the permanent slot model (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` = 6 shared weapon/power-up slots) and the victory-snapshot vocabulary from `AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ` (`DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`: permanent weapon levels, power-up levels, consumable pools). The bot is never flown; its loadout is stored data that feeds the one rating formula.
- **Hangar catalogue entries (producer Q3):** the upgrade pool is the shipped `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` — **weapons, hulls and modifiers** (producer Q10 = "everything") — no new economy, no new currency; ring gating and prices reused as authored, plus the new per-level weapon-upgrade price (Q9 = B).
- **Slot-fit rule (producer Q8 = A):** a weapon the bot does **not** already own is offered **only** when the bot has an empty permanent slot; a weapon the bot already carries is always offered as a level-upgrade. Hulls and modifiers have no slot requirement (a hull swaps `hullId`, a modifier applies its effect).
- **One interaction (producer Q4):** an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action in the hex summary section opens a version of the player-ship upgrade scene (the hangar screen) scoped to the bot — same screen pattern, different purchase target.
- **Destruction (producer Q5):** upgrades are persistent **unless** the hex loses a defence tick, which destroys the bot (today's `applyDefence` already unholds the hex and drops its defender; nothing new to build there).
- **Rating (producer Q6):** upgrades change the stored `defenceRating`, recomputed through the single shipped formula.
- **No player-ship effect (producer Q7):** a bot purchase never touches the player's deployed ship, active loadout or the fleet's owned sets.
- **No schema version bump:** new optional fields read by field presence, matching `skills` / `frontierTick`.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `HexDefender` (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) is a derived-rating record — `hullId`, `defenceRating`, `bankedMinerals`, optional `skills` — with no weapon slots or upgrade levels. It is never flown; every defence is arithmetic over stored numbers.
- The sibling item (AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ) lands the bot ship-model vocabulary in the economy: `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`, `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS` (one frozen row per `WeaponId`/`PowerUpId`), `defenderStatBuckets`, `snapshotDefenderUpgrades`, and `defenderRatingFromSnapshot` — already merged (commits `46d217b5`, `58dc8edc`). Its capture-cycle threading is being delivered through its own child items (e.g. AH-0MWHF6ZHW0058SMX); **this item depends on that snapshot existing on `HexDefender`** (dependency edge recorded).
- The player-ship slot model is the permanent six-slot pool shared by weapons and power-ups (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` in `src/core/constants.ts`, `capDropIdsToSlotPool` in `src/powerups/slots.ts`).
- The hangar economy (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) owns prices, `canBuy`/`buy`, `purchaseWeight`, ring gating and `resolvePlayerStrength`; the catalogue (`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`) holds hulls, starting weapons and modifiers with two-currency prices.
- The hangar screen (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) is the pure model + one renderer used by the shipped hangar scene **and** `GymHangar`; the hex map (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` + `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) renders focused-hex intel in the right-hand detail panel, with held hexes selectable but not actionable.
- Defence ticks (`runFrontierTick` → `applyDefence`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`) already destroy a fallen hex's defender (`held=false`, `defender=null`).

## Desired change

1. **Bot ship model.** `HexDefender` carries the shipped upgrade-snapshot vocabulary (permanent weapon/power-up levels, consumable pools) as additive optional fields, alongside the existing hull/rating/skills — the same-data-model rule (Q2). The bot's slot occupancy derives from the stored levels against `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`.
2. **Fit rule (pure).** A new pure function answers, per catalogue entry and per defender: `upgrade-existing` (bot already carries the weapon → level +1), `add-to-empty-slot` (new weapon kind, **only when a free slot exists**), `re-hull` (hull entry, no slot requirement), `train` (modifier entry, no slot requirement), or a disabled reason (slot pool full, unaffordable in either currency, ring-gated). The fit rule and the hangar's `canBuy` combine into one verdict per row.
3. **Per-level weapon-upgrade price (Q9 = B).** One authored table defines the upgrade price for raising an already-carried weapon's level (distinct from the catalogue's new-kind purchase price). Both prices appear on the row and are paid from the hangar wallet.
4. **Purchase application (pure).** Spending the displayed price applies the upgrade to the defender's ship: a new weapon kind enters at level 1 in one permanent slot, an already-carried weapon rises one level, a hull entry swaps `hullId` keeping the carried loadout, a modifier entry applies its effect; `defenceRating` recomputes through `defenderRatingFromSnapshot` / the buckets mapping — one formula (Q6). A refused purchase returns the payload unchanged.
5. **Map action.** The held-hex detail panel (the "hex summary section") gains an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action; `HexMapScene` wires it to open the bot-upgrade screen for the focused defender (Q4). Unheld hexes offer nothing; the gym's read-only render (no handlers) offers nothing — parity by construction.
6. **Bot-upgrade screen.** A hangar-screen-style scene scoped to one defender: same pure model + one renderer shape as `hangarScreen`, showing the fit verdicts, both price kinds and the bot's current loadout/rating; purchases return a fresh payload that the scene persists. Game and gym (if exercised) share the model/renderer so they cannot drift.
7. **Persistence and destruction.** Purchases persist via the versioned store (additive optional fields, field-presence parse). A defence-tick fall destroys the bot including its upgrades through the existing `applyDefence` path (Q5).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HexDefender` gains additive optional upgrade-snapshot fields (weapon/power-up levels, consumable pools) mirroring `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/botUpgrade.ts` (new) — the pure fit rule, the per-level upgrade-price table (Q9 = B), purchase application and per-row verdict for a defender's upgrade options (own module so the scenes never derive a fit).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — any shared helper the purchase needs (wallet spend, snapshot → rating via existing `defenderRatingFromSnapshot`).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — defensive parse/round-trip of the new optional fields (field presence).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` and `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — the held-hex `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action row + activation wiring in the detail panel.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — handler wiring (`onUpgradeDefences(hexId)` → open the bot-upgrade screen) and the route back after a purchase.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/botUpgradeScreen.ts` (new) + `src/scenes/hangarWar/botUpgradeScene.ts` (or a mode of the existing hangar screen) — the pure model + one renderer for the bot-upgrade screen.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` (and `GymHangar` if it renders the upgrade screen) — parity/no handlers for the new surface.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, README — the new control surface and its parity entry.

## Related work

- **Hangar War: leave the defending bot with the run's permanent upgrades (AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ)** — dependency: supplies the `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot` model, the stat-bucket mapping and the snapshot-aware rating this item's purchases consume; its capture-cycle threading first puts the snapshot on `HexDefender`.
- Hangar economy and unlock tree (AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6) — owns `canBuy`/`buy`, prices and ring gating the purchase path reuses.
- Capture cycle — hex deployment, boss-granted discovery and defending bot (AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6) — the module that creates `HexDefender`s.
- Hex-map intel / map screen (AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2) — the detail panel that gains the `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action.
- Post-MVP Hangar War: upgraded defending bots with special skills (AH-0MVWZYJ740037EZ1) — precedent for additive optional defender fields and the skills pattern (modifier `train` applies here).
- Versioned `ai_hell_hangar_war` store with migration (AH-0MVUXC0M5007LCGV) — the back-compat pattern new optional fields follow.
- Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal (AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP) — the tick path that destroys a fallen bot (Q5).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Balance risk (highest):** spendable upgrades let a player push a held hex's rating high, making well-defended hexes mathematically unretakeable — the same accepted consequence as the sibling item's Q3 = A. *Mitigation:* one rating formula and one mapping table, so a follow-up tuning item can cap or rescale prices without touching saves; measure from real runs before filing.
- **Pricing granularity risk (Q9 = B):** the per-level weapon-upgrade price is new authored data; its exact progression is a balance knob. *Mitigation:* one documented table in `botUpgrade.ts`, authorable without code changes; defaults chosen conservatively at implement time and reviewed in the effort/risk notes.
- **Dependency risk:** the brief assumes the sibling's snapshot-on-`HexDefender` threading lands first. If it slips, this item's data model cannot build. *Mitigation:* dependency edge recorded; implement after the sibling's capture threading.
- **Save-compatibility risk:** new optional fields must be omitted when empty and parsed defensively, or existing saves/fixtures drift. *Mitigation:* the `skills` pattern exactly; store round-trip + pre-change-save tests.
- **Wallet-conflict risk:** bot purchases spend the same banked minerals/cores the player uses for fleet unlocks — a bot spend can starve the hangar. *Deliberate per Q3/Q8 (A):* catalogue-priced, shared wallet; documented rather than gated in this item.
- **Modifier-fit risk (Q10 = everything):** a modifier whose effect targets run stats (e.g. `extra-lives`) has no bot meaning; only modifier effects with a stored-bot effect (e.g. `defence-skill`) can be sent. *Mitigation:* the fit rule classifies modifier effects by whether they change stored defender data; `extra-lives`-style effects are shown disabled with a reason rather than silently charged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** candidates deliberately excluded — a bot that is actually flown in combat, any new currency, new catalogue entries, and any change to player-ship progression or the frontier tuning constants. Each excluded candidate must become its own work item rather than growing this one.
- **Assumption (Q8, A):** the upgrade screen offers every catalogue entry the fleet can afford (ring + wallet gating), subject to the slot-fit rule for new weapons; a purchase spends banked salvage without granting the fleet an unlock — the bot gets the entry, the fleet does not.
- **Assumption (Q9, B):** a per-level upgrade-price table governs raising an already-carried weapon's level; a new weapon kind pays the catalogue purchase price and enters at level 1, occupying one permanent slot when one is free.
- **Assumption:** "permanent slots" for the bot mean the shared six-slot weapon/power-up pool (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`), counted by distinct permanently-carried kinds — the bot's stored data, never a live battle.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — "What does 'send upgrades for the ship' mean?" — **Answer (operator):** upgrade the **defending bot** (the bot left in the hex). *Source:* interactive reply.
- Q2 — "Does the bot get its own slot system?" — **Answer (operator):** the bot should be the **same as a player-controlled ship**, using the same data model so it has **slots etc.** *Research:* `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` (six shared weapon/power-up slots) and the sibling item's `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot` are the vocabularies this maps onto.
- Q3 — "What counts as an upgrade the player can send?" — **Answer (operator):** **hangar catalogue entries**, purchased with minerals and/or cores from the Hangar. *Research:* `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` + `canBuy`/`buy` already implement two-currency, ring-gated purchases.
- Q4 — "What's the UI interaction?" — **Answer (operator):** add an **"upgrade defenses" button to the hex summary section**, which opens **a version of the player-ship upgrade scene (hangar)** but upgrades the bot instead of the player's ship.
- Q5 — "Persistence and limits?" — **Answer (operator):** **persistent unless it loses a defence tick, in which case it is destroyed** (matches today's `applyDefence`: a fallen hex unholds and drops its defender).
- Q6 — "How does the upgrade affect the bot's defence?" — **Answer (operator):** it **changes the defence rating** (recomputed through the one shipped formula).
- Q7 — "Does sending upgrades affect the player's ship?" — **Answer (operator):** **no**.
- Q8 — "Which catalogue entries can the player send?" — **Answer (operator):** **A** — every catalogue entry the fleet can afford, spending banked salvage without granting the fleet an unlock — **refined**: a weapon the bot does **not** already own is offered **only** when the bot has an **empty slot**. *Source:* interactive reply (round 2).
- Q9 — "How does 'upgrade to an existing weapon' price?" — **Answer (operator):** **B** — a **separate per-level upgrade price** (its own authored pricing table), distinct from the catalogue purchase price for a new kind. *Source:* interactive reply (round 2).
- Q10 — "Which catalogue kinds are in scope?" — **Answer (operator):** **everything** — weapons, hulls and modifiers are all sendable (each with its own fit rule; hulls re-hull, modifiers apply their stored effect). *Source:* interactive reply (round 2).

# Tests: bot-upgrade fit-rule and purchase-economics contract (red-first)

Child of AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ (Strengthen a hexes defence). Red-first guard tests for the pure bot-upgrade contract — written first, RED until the `botUpgrade` module (its implementation sibling) lands. No implementation ships in this item; it pins the contract.

## Target outcome

A test-only item that locks the fit rule, the per-level upgrade price (Q9 = B), the purchase economics and the one-formula rating recompute so the pure module can be implemented (TDD) against a fixed contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fit-rule tests assert every authored verdict against `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`: `upgrade-existing` (the bot already carries the weapon → its level rises by one), `add-to-empty-slot` (a weapon kind the bot does not carry → offered **only** when at least one permanent slot is free), `re-hull` (a hull entry), `train` (a modifier entry whose effect changes stored defender data), and each disabled reason (slot pool full / unaffordable in either currency / ring-gated).
- Per-level upgrade-price tests assert the Q9 = B rule: raising an already-carried weapon's level costs the separate authored per-level price, distinct from the catalogue entry's purchase price for a new kind; both prices come from one pricing table.
- Purchase-economics tests assert a purchase spends exactly the displayed price from the hangar wallet (`HangarState.bankedMinerals` / `bankedCores`), applies the upgrade (a new weapon kind occupies one permanent slot at level 1; a carried weapon rises one level), and refused purchases (unaffordable / ring-gated / slot pool full) return the payload unchanged without touching the wallet.
- Rating tests assert a purchase recomputes `defenceRating` through `defenderRatingFromSnapshot` / `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS` — the one existing formula — and never a second derivation.
- Ship-isolation tests assert a bot purchase never mutates the fleet's owned sets, the active hull/loadout or the player's deployed ship (producer Q7).
- Tests cover: the fit rule (upgrade-existing vs add-to-empty-slot vs re-hull vs train vs disabled states), purchase economics (price, per-level upgrade price, wallet deduction, refused purchases) and snapshot update + rating recompute.
- Tests are RED until the pure `botUpgrade` module exists, then GREEN unchanged (contract stability).

## Constraints

- Pure-core only: no Phaser, no storage access, no scene imports in the tested module.
- The bot uses the same ship data model as a player-controlled ship (permanent slot model, `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`).

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` (existing — `HangarState`, `defenderRatingFromSnapshot`, `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS`)

## Dependencies

None upstream (writes tests first). Blocks the pure-module implementation child.

## Deliverables

- Red-first test suite for the bot-upgrade contract; documentation of the expected verdict/price/economics surface.

# Fade bullets out

## Problem statement

When an enemy bullet reaches the end of its range (its lifetime expires), it
currently **pops out of existence** — its sprite is destroyed in one frame.
Instead it should **shrink to nothing** during the last 20 % of its life, so
the expiry reads as a smooth visual dissolve rather than a snap. The bullet
remains dangerous while it shrinks.

## Users

- **Players** — as a player, I want enemy bullets to shrink away smoothly as
  they exhaust their range, so the game feel is polished and bullet expiry is
  readable at a glance instead of popping.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Shrink over the last 20 %:** an enemy bullet's view scales down
  from its full size to nothing during the final 20 % of its lifetime, and is
  destroyed when the lifetime elapses (as today).
- **AC2 — Full size before the fade window:** before the last 20 % of its
  lifetime the bullet renders at full scale (unchanged behaviour for the
  stored/lifetime bulk of its flight).
- **AC3 — Damages the player while shrinking:** the bullet's collision
  footprint keeps tracking its **visual sprite bounds** during the fade — it
  can still hit the player while visibly smaller, exactly until it fades away
  entirely.
- **AC4 — Enemy bullets only:** player bullets are **not** affected — their
  existing expiry behaviour is unchanged.
- **AC5 — Shared seam, gym↔game parity:** the change lands in the shared
  enemy-bullet lifecycle (`src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`), so the game
  and every gym scene that spawns enemy bullets fade identically; gyms that
  exercise enemy bullets cover the new behaviour.
- **AC6 — Testing:** automated unit tests verify the fade-window scaling
  (including a bullet destroyed exactly at expiry), no scaling outside the
  window, and that an animated (`redraw`) bullet fades too without regressing
  the per-frame animation hook.
- **AC7 — Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
  site entries.
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

Enemy bullets shrink smoothly to nothing as their range runs out instead of
popping away, while staying just as dangerous while they fade.

## Constraints

- The shared lifecycle helper `advanceWrappingBullets` is the single
  ownership point for enemy-bullet advance, wrap and expiry — every scene
  (game and gyms) consumes it, so behaviour must not diverge per scene
  (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1, gym↔game parity).
- The bullet view is now a **sprite of a cached texture**, not a Graphics
  object (AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF); scaling must go through the sprite's
  `setScale` (no per-frame redraw of the texture).
- Fade duration is **not** proportional to bullet size — it is a fixed
  20 % of the bullet's own lifetime (producer decision, Q3).
- The existing expiry must still destroy the sprite exactly when the
  lifetime elapses (tested by the current suite).
- Collision/hitbox: enemy bullets currently use a fixed radius
  (`getEnemyBulletRadius`, ~8 px); the fade must make the effective
  footprint follow the visual sprite bounds while shrinking (producer
  decision, Q5).

## Risks & assumptions

- The bullet view contract (`BulletView`) must gain a scale capability;
  every consumer — game, gyms and the test stub — needs the new member.
  Mitigation: extend the structural interface and the `StubEnemyBullet` in
  `bulletLifecycle.test.ts` in the same change (the test already drives the
  shape of the contract).
- Scale baseline assumption: full scale (1.0) is the bullet's baked sprite
  size; the fade interpolates from 1.0 to ~0 over the window regardless of
  the baked radius — no radius-proportional formula (producer decision Q3).
- Collision-footprint change must not regress the fixed-radius path for
  bullets outside the fade window (AC2) nor the bomb/clearing paths that
  iterate `getEnemyBullets()` (PlayScene 3532, 1792).
- Scope-creep guard: fade applies to enemy bullets only; anything further
  (e.g. player-bullet fades, alpha fades, radius-proportional timing) is
  recorded as a separate work item, not part of this one.

## Existing state

In `advanceWrappingBullets` (`src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`), each
enemy bullet advances, wraps at the four edges, optionally animates through
its `redraw` hook, and is destroyed the moment `elapsed >= lifetime` — the
sprite vanishes in one frame. Enemy-bullet collision against the player uses
`getEnemyBulletRadius()` in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`.

## Desired change

Inside `advanceWrappingBullets`, once the bullet enters its final 20 % of
lifetime, scale its view down smoothly from full size to zero (e.g. linearly
with the remaining time fraction) before destroying it at expiry. The
shrink must be observable through the same structural view contract every
scene and test uses, and the collision footprint must shrink with the visual.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` — `advanceWrappingBullets` (+ the
  `WrappingBullet` / `BulletView` structural interfaces; likely add a
  `setScale` capability to the view contract) — owns the fade-window scaling.
- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.test.ts` — unit tests for the fade
  window, no-scaling-outside-window, animated-bullet fade, expiry-at-zero.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `getEnemyBulletRadius()` /
  enemy-bullet-vs-player collision — make the hit radius track the fading
  sprite bounds.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/…` — consumers of
  `advanceWrappingBullets`; verify parity (no per-scene copies to change).
- `docs/…` — GDD §4.4 (bullet range/lifetime) / any visual-feel docs, if
  the fade deserves a mention.

## Related work

- AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0 — Bullets have a distance and wrap around the screen
  (lifetime/expiry model this builds on; completed).
- AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF — Cache bullet shapes as textures and batch bullet
  draw submission (sprite-of-cached-texture view; completed).
- AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA — shared bullet-lifecycle extraction parent
  (the helper this changes; completed).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity convention (shared seam
  requirement; completed).
- AH-0MVT2W5EL004OXNN — Eval arena wrap parity (bullet lifetime expiry
  preserved; completed).
- AH-0MUL15N63003PUDB — Animate enemies gliding to their re-anchored
  formation slots (smooth-motion/tweening precedent; completed).
- AH-0MV70Y2XY005J2HI — Hold-full overlay: fade the thruster/engine hum out
  while paused (fade precedent; completed).

### Related work (automated report)

Generated by `/skill:find-related` (imported into this brief): repository
keyword matches in `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` and
`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (bullets/damage/range/fade/shrink
terms). Full report:
`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MWJ9PMYF005N588.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — Fade mechanism: reduce alpha, scale, or both? — Answer (producer):
  **scale only**. Research: cached-texture sprites support `setScale`
  directly (AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF); alpha fades are used elsewhere (pulse
  wave §7.2) but the producer chose shrink-by-scale for bullets.
- Q2 — When does the fade begin? — Answer (producer): **the last 20 % of
  the bullet's life**. Fixed fraction of lifetime, not a fixed time.
- Q3 — Fade duration proportional to initial size? — Answer (producer):
  **ignore** — stick to the last 20 % of life for every bullet regardless of
  size. Note: this supersedes the original description's "duration of the
  shrink should be proportional to their initial size". Prior
  answer/description text updated in this brief.
- Q4 — Player bullets? — Answer (producer): **enemy only**.
- Q5 — Hitbox during the fade — Answer (producer): **visual sprite bounds**;
  the bullet can still damage the player while shrinking, exactly until it
  fades to nothing.
