# Hangar power-up ownership has no source

## Problem statement

The pure upgrade rule treats a power-up as **owned** only when the hangar records it, but no shipped path ever records one — the run's power-up levels are run-scoped and never reach the hangar, the hex-grant seam does not know power-up ids, and the unlock tree sells only hulls, weapons and modifiers. So the buy-to-upgrade economy can only ever upgrade weapons in real play.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want to **buy a power-up in the hangar tree** with banked minerals/cores so that my fleet permanently owns it between runs, I can then spend salvage raising its permanent level, and the ship I deploy with starts with it.

## Impact

Players can buy power-ups in the hangar and keep them between runs, so the hangar's power-up upgrade rows finally mean something — spend salvage, own a power-up, upgrade it, deploy with it.

## Users

- **The hangar player** — sees power-up rows in the unlock tree, buys one with banked salvage, and later upgrades it (`As a player I want a power-up I own in the hangar, not just a 10-second drop`).
- **The defending-bot player** — a defender left after those upgrades inherits the higher permanent level through the existing capture snapshot.
- **The gym maintainer** — `GymHangar` buys the same entry through the same pure rule and the same store write (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md).

## Producer decisions (2026-11-17)

- **Q1 = (b) hangar tree/shop entry.** Power-ups become purchasable unlock-tree entries; a purchase is what creates the hangar's first permanent level row. The hex-grant route and the run-carry-over route are **not** taken (the hex boss keeps granting hulls, weapons and modifiers only).
- **Q2 = (ii) explicit owned set.** `HangarState` gains `unlockedPowerUps` as the canonical ownership record (mirroring `unlockedWeapons`), and `costToUpgrade`/`buyUpgrade` read power-up ownership from it. A persisted `hangar.powerUpLevels` row still implies ownership, so no stored row is orphaned.
- **Q3 = (1) author the shipped content here.** This item authors at least one buyable, ring-gated, level-bearing power-up entry so a fresh save can own one in normal play — a seam nobody calls would be the same bug again.

## Existing state (evidence)

- **The rule.** `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — `costToUpgrade`/`buyUpgrade` decide ownership per kind (`ownsUpgradeableKind`): weapons via `hangar.unlockedWeapons`, power-ups via a `levels.powerUps` row. Non-level-bearing kinds are refused `non-upgradeable` (producer Q2 = (a) of AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU), and the ceiling is `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL = 5`.
- **Persistence exists but is unmerged.** Commit `ec62c313` on branch `wl-AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH-persist-permanent-levels-through-store-a` adds `hangar.weaponLevels` / `hangar.powerUpLevels` (optional, field-presence migrated), `buyHangarUpgrade`, and the deploy-time grant in `hangarDeployment.ts`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor ec62c313 dev` is **false**, and `dev`'s `parseHangar` parses no level fields — so this item is gated by that branch landing.
- **The tree has no power-ups.** `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — `HangarEntryKind` is `'hull' | 'weapon' | 'modifier'`, `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` is documented as *six buyable entries* plus two starter entries, and `HangarEntry` has no power-up member. `HangarState` has no `unlockedPowerUps` (no such identifier exists in `src/`).
- **Purchase plumbing is generic.** `canBuy` (precedence `owned` → `gated` → `unaffordable`), `buy`, `ownsEntry` and `ownedIds` are kind-driven, so a new kind is a small, compiler-enforced change (`ownedIds` is an exhaustive switch); `buildHangarUnlockRows` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) already renders **every** purchasable catalogue entry with the existing `BUY`/`OWNED`/`RING N`/`NEED N min` vocabulary, so the row is nearly free.
- **Two generic catalogue consumers would move with it.** `cheapestUsefulUnlock` (`hangarEconomy.ts`) and `cheapestSeededUnlock` (`src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts`) both scan the whole catalogue, and `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` reports unlock pace over `isPurchasableEntry` entries whose numbers are pinned in docs.
- **Run levels are run-scoped.** `Player.getPowerUpLevels()` reads the run's single `PowerUpLevelStore`; GDD §4.4 states permanence is *scoped to the run* and nothing writes those rows into the hangar.

## Desired change

Power-ups become a fourth unlock-tree kind whose ownership lives in a new persisted `hangar.unlockedPowerUps` set; buying one spends the two-currency price, records ownership **and** seeds its `hangar.powerUpLevels` row at level 1 in one payload write, so the existing upgrade rule and deploy grant work unchanged. At least one level-bearing power-up is authored for sale.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. The producer decision is reflected in the design record: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.1/§8.2 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D state that a hangar power-up is **bought from the unlock tree**, owned in `hangar.unlockedPowerUps`, and upgraded by the buy-to-upgrade rule; the `hangarEconomy.ts` comment calling a `powerUpLevels` row *"the only place the hangar records a power-up level"* is corrected to separate level from ownership.
- 2. `HangarEntryKind` gains `'power-up'` with an entry type carrying the shipped `PowerUpId`, name, description, two-currency `HangarPrice`, `minRing` and `starter`, and `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` authors **at least one** level-bearing permanent power-up (from bomb, speed_boost, magnet, mineral_scoop, smart_bomb, frenzy, chrono, salvage, strike, mining_laser) for sale at a reachable ring; consumables and the field-pickup-only kind are never authored as level entries.
- 3. `HangarState` gains `unlockedPowerUps` as the canonical ownership record and the versioned store persists it: parsed defensively (non-list values, duplicates and unusable ids collapse exactly like `unlockedWeapons`), absent in a pre-change save and reading as "owns none" (field-presence migration, **no schema version bump**), and empty in `createDefaultPayload`.
- 4. Buying a power-up through `buy` spends its price, adds the id to `unlockedPowerUps` **and** seeds its `hangar.powerUpLevels` row at `level` 1 in one payload write, so `getPowerUpLevels()` and the deploy grant see it on the very next deployment; a refused purchase changes neither field and spends nothing.
- 5. `costToUpgrade`/`buyUpgrade` read power-up ownership from `unlockedPowerUps` (a persisted level row also implies ownership); an unowned power-up is still refused `unowned`, the purchased one offers and buys the next level through the store's `buyHangarUpgrade`, and the deploy path grants the raised level onto the run `Player`.
- 6. The hangar screen renders the new entries through the shared renderer as ordinary unlock rows using the **existing** `BUY`/`OWNED`/`RING N`/`NEED N min` states and labels (no new row state invented); the owned-row **upgrade** affordance remains AH-0MWI5AK1E008HDDH's scope; `GymHangar` shows the same rows and buys through the same store write.
- 7. The attract/traversal bot's purchase candidates keep their current kind set (power-up entries are excluded from the bot's choice by one documented helper), so `cheapestUsefulUnlock`/`decideHangarAction` behaviour, `cheapestSeededUnlock` replays and the pinned `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` unlock-pace numbers are unchanged; if the producer prefers the bot to buy power-ups, the affected reports and docs are regenerated in the same change (see Assumptions).
- 8. Tests cover: the new catalogue entry's typing and purchase (price, `gated`, `unaffordable`, `owned` refusal), first level row created by a purchase, upgrade of the now-owned power-up end to end through the store, save/load round-trip of the owned set and the level row, a pre-change save loading with no power-ups and no rows, refusal of a consumable/field-pickup-only id, and the screen's unlock-row states for the new kind.
- 9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- 10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **One ownership record per kind.** `unlockedPowerUps` is canonical; `hangar.powerUpLevels` carries levels only. No third representation, and no parallel ownership check outside `ownedIds`/`ownsUpgradeableKind`.
- **Atomic persistence.** Ownership and the seeded level row land in one `saveHangarWarPayload` write, so a saved purchase can never own a power-up without its level (or the reverse).
- **Level-bearing kinds only.** Consumables (charge pools) and `extra_life` (`fieldPickupOnly`) are never sold as levels; the completed rule's `non-upgradeable` refusal stands and must be covered by a test.
- **Field-presence migration, no schema bump.** `unlockedPowerUps` is additive and optional in the stored payload; absence reads as "owns none".
- **Compiler-enforced kinds.** `ownedIds`/`ownsEntry` must gain the new member through the exhaustive switch — no `default:` fallback that could silently un-own a kind.
- **Loadout and grants untouched.** `resolveActiveLoadout` continues to consider only weapons and modifiers (a power-up entry never becomes a starting weapon); hex grants keep resolving to hulls/weapons/modifiers and the `GRANT_ONLY_MIN_RING` sentinel pattern is unchanged.
- **Economy conventions.** Price is the existing `HangarPrice` (minerals + cores), gating is `minRing`, and `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL` stays the single ceiling — no new currency, no second cap.
- **Gym↔game parity.** The pure rule, the renderer and the store write are shared; `GymHangar` gains no divergent copy (duplicate-body guard green).
- **Scope boundary.** The owned-row upgrade affordance is AH-0MWI5AK1E008HDDH; consumable charge purchases, a full pricing pass over all ten kinds, and hex-granted power-ups are separate items.
- **Dependency.** Gated by AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH merging to `dev` (branch `wl-AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH-…`, commit `ec62c313`); without it there is no persisted level field or deploy grant to write into.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — the `'power-up'` kind, the new entry type and the authored sellable power-up(s); the "six buyable entries" comment.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HangarState.unlockedPowerUps` (persisted contract).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — defensive parse of the new set, `createDefaultPayload`, and the purchase write path that seeds the level row.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — `ownedIds`, `ownsEntry`, `buy` (seed the level row), `ownsUpgradeableKind` (read the set); the corrected "only place" comment.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — unlock-row rendering for the new kind (shared renderer).
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — the purchase handler persisting through the store.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` — gym parity for the buy row.
- `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` / `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — the documented bot-candidate exclusion helper.
- Tests: `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts`, `hangarWarStore.test.ts`, `hangarScreen`/`HangarScene` tests, `src/ai/eval/ringTiming` tests.

## Assumptions

- **A1 — the attract/traversal bot does not buy power-ups** (AC7): keeps demo decisions, seeded traversal replays and the pinned ring-timing unlock-pace tables stable. Override welcome; then those reports/docs are regenerated here.
- **A2 — authored set and prices**: at least one, recommended 2–3 entries across rings 1–2, priced with the existing two-currency conventions above the starter unlocks; `starter: false` (no free power-up).
- **A3 — a purchase grants level 1**, the rule's own vocabulary, leaving four purchasable steps below `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL = 5`.
- **A4 — deploy grant** (`applyHangarWarDeployment`) lands with AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH; this item only supplies the rows it grants.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — pinned-report drift.** GDD §8.1's "six buyable entries", `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` unlock-pace tables, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` tables and README counts all describe the tree; a new kind changes what they report. Mitigation: A1's exclusion plus updating every affected doc/report in the same change.
- **Risk — two-field consistency.** A set entry without a level row, or a level row without a set entry, would make ownership and level disagree. Mitigation: seed on purchase, union in the ownership read, round-trip test.
- **Risk — save-shape test churn.** Byte-for-byte payload round-trip tests will need the new empty field's expectation; the field must be omitted-on-empty or explicitly expected, consistently.
- **Risk — unmerged dependency.** AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH is unmerged; building against `dev` today would fork the store path. Mitigation: blocked until it lands (dependency edge recorded).
- **Risk — scope creep.** Pricing all ten kinds, consumable charge sales and hex-granted power-ups are tempting adjacent work. Mitigation: file separately, author the minimum here.
- **Risk — catalogue consumers.** `ringTiming`, `hangarWarTraversal` and `cheapestUsefulUnlock` iterate the whole catalogue; an unguarded new kind silently changes AI/eval behaviour. Mitigation: the A1 exclusion is tested.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH** (discovered-from) — persisted permanent levels + deploy grant; **blocking dependency** (branch unmerged).
- **AH-0MWI5AAVO009UROY** — the pure upgrade rule (completed; its ownership read changes to the new set here).
- **AH-0MWI5AK1E008HDHH** — hangar owned-row upgrade affordance (depends on this item for a row to upgrade).

## Plan (2026-11-17)

Effort/risk pre-check: **Medium / Medium** → planning required. Plan-approval gate:
`request_approval: false` (not Extra Large + High/Severe), so no approval pause.

### Decomposition (test-first, dependency order)

   The whole contract pinned before implementation: catalogue typing and purchase
   states, the seeded level-1 row, the ownership union read, store round-trip and
   pre-change-save migration, screen row states, gym parity, deploy grant.
2. **Power-up unlock-tree kind, owned set and authored entry** —
   AH-0MWKXPO5A007R5RB (feature). `HangarEntryKind` + `PowerUpUnlockDefinition` +
   the authored sellable power-up(s); `HangarState.unlockedPowerUps` and its
   field-presence persistence; the two exhaustive switches; the shared renderer's
   rows. Vertical slice: show the row → buy → own it → save/load.
3. **Purchase seeds the level-1 row and the upgrade rule reads the owned set** —
   AH-0MWKXPUGF004RACW (feature). The bug's fix: `buy` seeds
   `hangar.powerUpLevels` at level 1 in the same payload write, and
   `ownsUpgradeableKind` reads `unlockedPowerUps` ∪ a persisted row, so
   purchase → upgrade → deploy works end to end.
4. **Keep power-ups out of the bot's choice and the pinned pace reports** —
   AH-0MWKXQ073003ULDX (task). One documented exclusion helper shared by

### Dependency edges

### Vertical-slice check

Each phase cuts every layer: (2) data → contract type → store → pure rule → renderer
→ tests; (3) pure rule → store write → deployment grant → tests; (4) data predicate →
AI/eval consumers → pinned tests; (5) docs; (6) gate. No phase is a single horizontal

- **A7 — the owned-row `UPGRADE` affordance comes for free.** `buildUpgradeAffordance`

# Power-up ownership contract tests (red-first)

## Purpose

Pin the **whole** power-up-ownership contract before any implementation child
starts, so the catalogue kind, the persisted owned set, the seeded level-1 row
and the upgrade read are all driven by failing tests rather than written first
and blessed afterwards. Every assertion names the behaviour it pins; a test that
would pass against today's `dev` is only kept where it pins unchanged existing
behaviour (the "no regression" half of the contract).

Producer decisions recorded on the parent: Q1 = (b) hangar tree/shop entry,
Q2 = (ii) explicit `unlockedPowerUps` owned set, Q3 = (1) author the shipped
content here. A1 = the attract/traversal bot keeps its current purchase kinds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts` asserts the new `'power-up'` catalogue
  entry: its `kind` is `'power-up'`, its id is a shipped `PowerUpId`, it carries a
  two-currency `HangarPrice`, `minRing`, `starter: false`, and its id is neither a
  consumable nor the field-pickup-only kind (read from `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts` asserts `canBuy` for a power-up
  entry returns `gated` below `minRing`, `unaffordable` with the exact shortfall,
  and `owned` once owned; a successful `buy` spends both currencies, adds the id
  to `hangar.unlockedPowerUps` **and** seeds a `hangar.powerUpLevels` row with
  `level: 1`; a refused `buy` changes neither field and spends nothing.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts` asserts `costToUpgrade` refuses an
  unowned power-up `unowned`, treats a persisted `powerUpLevels` row (with no
  owned-set entry) as ownership, and that `buyUpgrade` raises the level by one
  toward `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts` asserts the `non-upgradeable`
  refusal still stands for a consumable id and for the field-pickup-only id.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts` asserts a save/load round-trip of
  `hangar.unlockedPowerUps` together with its `powerUpLevels` row, that
  `createDefaultPayload` carries an empty owned set, that a pre-change save (no
  owned-set field) loads as "owns none" with no level rows and no schema-version
  bump, and that non-list values, duplicates and unusable ids collapse exactly
  like `unlockedWeapons`.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` (the `buildHangarUnlockRows` suite) and
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` assert the new kind's unlock-row states
  through the shared renderer (`BUY`, `RING N`, `NEED N min`, `OWNED`) using the
  existing labels, that a purchase persists through exactly one
  `saveHangarWarPayload` write, and that `GymHangar`'s read-only summary lists the
  same row.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.test.ts` asserts a bought power-up's
  seeded level reaches `HangarWarDeployment.powerUpLevels`, and that a raised
  level is what `applyHangarWarDeployment` grants onto the run `Player`.
- The suite is committed **red** (or skipped-with-reason where an assertion
  cannot compile yet) before the implementation children begin, and each
  implementation child flips its own assertions green.
- Tests use the shared fixtures and existing seams (`HangarEntry`, injected
  catalogues, in-memory storage) — no new test-only production export.

- Tests cover: the new catalogue entry's typing and purchase (price, `gated`,
  `unaffordable`, `owned` refusal), first level row created by a purchase, upgrade
  of the now-owned power-up end to end through the store, save/load round-trip of
  the owned set and the level row, a pre-change save loading with no power-ups and
  no rows, refusal of a consumable/field-pickup-only id, and the screen's
  unlock-row states for the new kind.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the existing test files rather than adding new ones where the sibling
  suites already cover the same module (catalogue, economy, store, screen,
  deployment).
- Author the failing assertions first, then hand the green work to the
  implementation children in dependency order.
- Assert through public seams only (`canBuy`, `buy`, `costToUpgrade`,
  `buyUpgrade`, `buyHangarUpgrade`, `parseHangarWarPayload`,
  `buildHangarUnlockRows`, `buildHangarDeployment`).

## Dependencies

None — this is the test-first entry point. Blocks all implementation children.

## Key Files

- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarSlice.integration.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts`

## Deliverables

Parent: AH-0MWKT12BT001106T — the purchase creates the first permanent level row.

# Purchase seeds the level-1 row and the upgrade rule reads the owned set

## Purpose

Close the reported bug: a purchase must create the power-up's **first permanent
level row** (producer Q2 = (ii), A3), so the existing buy-to-upgrade rule offers
a next level and the deploy grant hands the level to the run. Both the owned set
and the seeded row land in **one** payload write.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `buy` seeds `hangar.powerUpLevels` with `{ id, level: 1 }` for a power-up
  purchase in the same returned hangar that carries the ownership entry and the
  spent currency, so `purchaseHangarEntry`'s one `saveHangarWarPayload` write
  persists both fields together — a saved purchase can never own a power-up
  without its level, or the reverse.
- A refused purchase seeds no row, adds no ownership entry and spends nothing.
- `ownsUpgradeableKind` reads a power-up as owned from `hangar.unlockedPowerUps`
  **union** a persisted `powerUpLevels` row (a row written by an older save still
  implies ownership, so no stored row is orphaned); there is no third
  representation and no ownership check outside `ownedIds`/`ownsUpgradeableKind`.
- An unowned power-up is still refused `unowned`; the just-purchased one offers
  and buys its next level through `hangarWarStore.buyHangarUpgrade`
  (`upgradeHangarKind`), raising the level by exactly one with `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL`
  as the single ceiling (level 1 after purchase leaves four purchasable steps).
- The chain purchase → seeded row → upgrade → deploy is proven end to end:
  `buildHangarDeployment` carries the bought and raised levels in
  `HangarWarDeployment.powerUpLevels`, and `applyHangarWarDeployment` grants them
  onto the run `Player`.
- The `hangarEconomy.ts` comment calling a `powerUpLevels` row "the only place the
  hangar records a power-up level" is corrected to separate **level** from
  **ownership** (ownership = `unlockedPowerUps`), matching the persisted
  contract's documentation.
- The red-first assertions owned by this slice pass, including the
  `non-upgradeable` refusal for a consumable and the field-pickup-only id.

- Buying a power-up through `buy` spends its price, adds the id to
  `unlockedPowerUps` and seeds its `hangar.powerUpLevels` row at `level` 1 in one
  payload write, so the deploy grant sees it on the very next deployment; a
  refused purchase changes neither field and spends nothing.
- `costToUpgrade`/`buyUpgrade` read power-up ownership from `unlockedPowerUps`
  (a persisted level row also implies ownership); an unowned power-up is still
  refused `unowned`, the purchased one offers and buys the next level through the
  store's `buyHangarUpgrade`, and the deploy path grants the raised level onto the
  run `Player`.

## Minimal Implementation

- Seed the row inside the pure `buy` (one place, next to the owned-set push),
  reusing the existing row vocabulary rather than a new helper or a second write.
- Change `ownsUpgradeableKind`'s power-up branch to
  `hangar.unlockedPowerUps.includes(id) || levels.powerUps.some(...)`; leave the
  weapon branch and every refusal class untouched.
- Add no new store function: `buyHangarUpgrade`, `withPermanentLevels` and
  `hangarPermanentLevels` already carry the row through the payload.
- Leave the UI affordance untouched — `buildUpgradeAffordance` is id-driven, so
  the owned row's `UPGRADE` state comes from the shared renderer.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the catalogue-kind / owned-set slice. Blocks the docs slice.

## Key Files

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`

## Deliverables

- The seeded level-1 row, the union ownership read, the corrected comment and the
  end-to-end purchase → upgrade → deploy tests.
data.title: Purchase seeds the level-1 row and the upgrade rule reads the owned set

# Keep power-ups out of the bot's choice and the pinned pace reports

## Purpose

The attract/traversal bot's purchase candidates must keep their current kind set
(A1), so demo decisions, seeded traversal replays and the pinned ring-timing
unlock-pace numbers do not move just because the catalogue grew. One documented
helper owns the exclusion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One documented helper (e.g. `isBotPurchasableEntry(entry)` beside
  `isPurchasableEntry` in `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`) is the **single**
  definition of "the bot may shop this", and it excludes the new `'power-up'`
  kind.
- `cheapestUsefulUnlock` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) and
  `cheapestSeededUnlock` (`src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts`) both consult that one
  helper — no duplicated predicate — so `decideHangarAction` and every seeded
  traversal replay produce their current results.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`'s unlock-pace numbers for the pre-existing
  catalogue entries are byte-identical; the report's new power-up rows are pinned
  explicitly in its tests (no silent total or count drift), and any doc or report
  that states a tree count is either unchanged or updated with the reason.
- The helper is tested both ways: a power-up entry is excluded from the bot's
  candidates while a hull / weapon / modifier entry at the same ring and price
  still qualifies, and a hand-authored test catalogue proves the exclusion is
  kind-driven rather than id-driven.
- The exclusion rationale (the bot buys the cheapest **useful** unlock; power-ups
  are a player choice, not a demo-scripted buy) is recorded in the helper's doc
  comment so a future reader can override it deliberately.

- The attract/traversal bot's purchase candidates keep their current kind set
  (power-up entries are excluded from the bot's choice by one documented helper),
  so `cheapestUsefulUnlock`/`decideHangarAction` behaviour, `cheapestSeededUnlock`
  replays and the pinned `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` unlock-pace numbers are
  unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add the helper in the catalogue module (pure data + one predicate) and route the
  two candidate scans through it.
- Leave `isPurchasableEntry` — which the hangar renderer and the unlock-pace
  report use — untouched, so the screen still lists power-ups for sale.
- Extend the existing traversal, economy and ringTiming tests rather than adding
  new suites.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the catalogue-kind / owned-set slice (the kind must exist before it
can be excluded). Blocks the verification slice.

## Key Files

- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`
- `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`
- `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.test.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- The documented bot-candidate exclusion, the pinned-report tests and the
  unchanged demo/traversal behaviour.

# Intake brief — Hex Map Information UX (AH-0MWL4QCVD007WOAM)

## Headline

The Hex Map screen (`HexMapScene`) draws roughly fifteen separately positioned
text objects and a ring of tiles with **no sectioning at all**: war status,
transient "what just happened" news, the map itself, the selected hex's intel and
the controls legend all float over the same background, in three different
columns and two different font conventions. This item introduces named,
visually bounded **sections** — each with its own heading — so every group of
information is distinguishable at a glance.

## Problem statement

There is a lot of information on the Hex Map and too little structure holding it
apart. Measured against the shipped renderer (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`,
960×540), the screen currently carries:

| What is drawn | Where it sits today |
|---|---|
| Screen title, and the run result line (`RUN: VICTORY · score N`) | centred, top (`y=18`, `y=46`) |
| Ring progress (`RING 2 — 3/12 HEXES HELD`) | left column (`x=24`, `y=62`) |
| Frontier strength (`FRONTIER · STR n · BEAT ≤ m (k IN REACH)`) | left column (`y=82`) |
| Hangar fleet + bank (`HANGAR · hull · n min · n cores`) | left column (`y=102`) |
| `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` panel (rolled-in defence report) | left column (`y=118`, conditional) |
| `HANGAR ASSAULT` banner (ring won / hangar falls) | left column (`y=300`, conditional) |
| `◀ HANGAR` action row | left column (`y=468`) |
| `READ THE MAP` legend, six lines of static help | right column (`y=112`–`y=182`) |
| `SELECTED HEX — FULL INTEL` detail panel | right column (`y=200`) |
| Hex tiles (`AGG n` + ownership marker + `(q,r)`), attack arrows, hangar marker | centre |
| Keyboard hint line | bottom centre (`y=530`) |

Three problems follow from that inventory:

1. **Unlike information is adjacent, like information is apart.** The three
   left-hand header lines mix ring progress, frontier combat maths and hangar
   inventory with no heading to separate them, while the two halves of "the
   selected hex" (its intel, right column; its attack row, left column) sit on
   opposite sides of the screen.
2. **Transient news has no home.** The run result is centred at the top, the
   hangar-assault outcome is a left-hand banner, and the banked win-bonus line
   (`model.winBonusLine`) is computed but **never drawn at all** — its only
   consumer is the `getWinBonusLine()` test seam. "What just happened" therefore
   arrives in up to three different places, one of which is nowhere.
3. **Help competes with content.** A six-line static legend occupies the top of
   the same right-hand column as the dynamic intel panel it explains, so the
   loudest text in that column is documentation rather than information about
   the player's war.

## Users

- **The Hangar War player** landing on the map between sorties.
  - *As a player, I want the map's status, my last sortie's outcome, the ring
    itself and the selected hex's intel each in their own labelled section, so I
    can find one thing without reading everything.*
  - *As a player, I want to know what just happened (victory/defeat, ring won or
    hangar falls, minerals banked) in one place, so I do not have to hunt three
    corners of the screen for the aftermath of my deployment.*
  - *As a player reading the selected hex, I want its intel and its attack row
    together, so one hex is one story rather than two panels apart.*
  - *As a colour-blind player, I want sections distinguished by headings and
    framing rather than by colour alone, consistent with the map's existing
    CVD-safe conventions.*
- **The maintainer** of the shared `buildHexMapModel` → `renderHexMap` pair,
  who needs the section layout to live in one renderer so the game and the
  `GymHexWar` parity gym cannot drift (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).

## Producer decisions (2026-11-17)

- **Q1 = (a)** — sections are **bordered, headed panels** laid out in fixed
  columns; every section has a frame, a heading and a bounded rect.
- **Q2 = (b)** — **four content sections plus a controls footer**: WAR STATUS,
  LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX (intel **and** its attack row together), and
  CONTROLS/LEGEND.
- **Q3 = (a)** — the banked win-bonus line **is rendered**, inside LAST SORTIE.

## Section model (producer-approved)

Four content sections plus a controls footer, each drawn as a **bordered,
headed panel** with a bounded rect:

| Section | Contains | Visibility |
|---|---|---|
| `war-status` | ring progress, frontier strength / beatable ceiling / in-reach count, hangar hull + banked minerals/cores | always |
| `last-sortie` | run result line, banked win bonus, hangar-assault outcome (`RING WON…` / `HANGAR FALLS…`) | only when the landing carries one of those |
| `map` | the ring tiles, attack arrows and hangar marker | always |
| `selected-hex` | the focused hex's full intel **and** its `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` row | always (panel body may be empty when nothing is focused) |
| `controls` | keyboard hint line + the `READ THE MAP` legend | always |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Section registry on the shared view.** `HexMapView` publishes a `sections`
  list — `{ key, heading, rect }` per rendered section — and every rendered text
  object, tile and arrow lies inside **exactly one** section rect, with no two
  section rects overlapping and every rect inside the 960×540 frame.
- **Every section is a bordered, headed panel (Q1 = a).** Each of `war-status`,
  `last-sortie` (when shown), `map`, `selected-hex` and `controls` draws a panel
  frame and one heading from a shared exported constant (`WAR STATUS`,
  `LAST SORTIE`, `SELECTED HEX`, `CONTROLS`, and the map's own title), in one
  consistent style and position convention, so the groupings are distinguishable
  without relying on colour.
- **No information is lost.** Every string the current renderer draws still
  renders, in its new section; the tile labels (`AGG n`, ownership marker,
  `(q,r)`), arrows, hint line and legend text are unchanged in content.
- **Transient news is grouped and complete (Q2 = b, Q3 = a).** The run result
  line, the hangar-assault banner and the banked win-bonus line
  (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`, from `model.winBonusLine`) render **only**
  inside `last-sortie`; the win-bonus line is now actually drawn, not merely
  queryable. When the landing carries none of the three, the section is absent
  (no empty headed box).
- **One hex, one section.** The selected hex's intel and its attack row render
  inside the same `selected-hex` section; the attack row is hidden (not moved to
  another section) when the focused hex is in no attack.
- **Help no longer competes with content.** The `READ THE MAP` legend moves into
  the `controls` section and no longer occupies the intel column.
- **Legibility at 960×540.** No section body text overdraws a hex tile or the
  hangar marker; long strings (draw name, assault arithmetic) word-wrap inside
  their section; no rendered text is smaller than today's smallest (9px) and
  headings are at least 10px.
- **Game/gym parity, one shared layout.** All layout lives in
  `renderHexMap`/`hexMap.ts`; `GymHexWar` renders the same sections read-only
  through the same call, and no gym-local or scene-local layout exists (the
  existing `renderHexMap` equivalence assertions stay green).
- **Interaction contract unchanged.** Grid arrow navigation, Tab/Shift+Tab
  cycling, Enter/Space inspect-or-deploy, tile hover/click, the `◀ HANGAR` row
  and ESC-to-menu behave exactly as before; the attract traversal still takes
  exactly one next action and cannot stall on a section.
- **Regression coverage.** `HexMapScene.test.ts`, the renderer/`hexIntel` tests
  and `GymHexWar.test.ts` pin the section registry (keys, headings, non-overlap,
  in-frame), `last-sortie` visibility toggling, and that the selected-hex intel
  and attack row share a section; position-only pins may be updated, behaviour
  pins may not be weakened.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries** — GDD §8.2 (the
  map's screen surface), the `hexMap.ts` module docblock, and
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` if its row description changes.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A Hangar War player can read the map at a glance: the war's status, the last
sortie's outcome, the ring itself, the selected hex's intel and the controls each
sit in their own labelled section instead of scattering across three columns.

## Constraints

- **Renderer-only change.** The model (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) stays
  the single source of every string; `hexMap.ts` only draws and positions. No
  gameplay rule, resolver call or persisted state is added.
- **One layout for game and gym.** The gym↔game parity contract and the existing
  `renderHexMap` equivalence assertions forbid a second layout implementation.
- **Single 960×540 viewport.** No scrolling, panning, tabs or collapsible
  sections unless the producer chooses the tabbed option in Q1.
- **Transient launch data stays transient** — run result, tick record, assault
  and win bonus are never persisted; a later entry renders no `last-sortie`.
- **Existing CVD-safe conventions hold** — section distinction must not depend on
  colour; the tile ownership encoding (blue/orange + filled/hollow marker) is
  untouched.
- **No new assets or fonts** — monospace text and Phaser Graphics panels only.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` (951 lines) holds every layout constant
  (`PANEL_X`, `ATTACK_PANEL_Y`, `ASSAULT_BANNER_Y`, legend rows, hint line) and
  draws all of the inventory above. There is no section abstraction: each text
  object is positioned by a hand-tuned literal.
- `HexMapView` already exposes behavioural seams (`getRows`, `getArrows`,
  `getPanelText`, `getLeftPanelText`, `getAssaultText`, …) but nothing describing
  screen regions, so no test can currently assert grouping or non-overlap.
- `model.winBonusLine` exists (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` →
  `defenceReport.ts`) and is surfaced only by `HexMapScene.getWinBonusLine()`;
  the renderer never draws it.
- Prior work already fixed the map's *readability* (reveal filter, CVD-safe tiles,
  coordinates, titled detail-panel lines) and its *navigation* (grid arrows), so
  this item is the remaining structural/visual-hierarchy step.

## Desired change

A sectioned Hex Map: a small number of named, bounded regions with headings, each
holding one kind of information, drawn by the shared renderer so the game and the
parity gym stay identical; transient sortie news gathered into one place; the
selected hex's intel and attack row brought together; help demoted to a controls
footer.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — the whole layout: section rects, headings,
  legend relocation, last-sortie grouping; add `sections` to `HexMapView`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — shared section-heading constants and any
  model wiring for the last-sortie lines (`winBonusLine` is already published)
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — query seam for `sections`, transient launch data
  plumbing (no rule change)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — renders the same sections read-only
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` — section/grouping pins; update
  position-only assertions
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — describe the
  sectioned map surface

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed): the
  scene and its intel model this item re-lays-out.
- **AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U** — Hangar Map UX (completed, parent): reveal filter,
  CVD-safe ownership, coordinates on tiles, spatial arrows — the readability and
  navigation pass that precedes this structural one.
- **AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK** — Hangar Map UI: clearer overview (completed): titled
  every line of the selected-hex intel. Its line titles are load-bearing for
  this item's `selected-hex` section and must not be disturbed.
- **AH-0MWEWYUAS002P7P9** — Renderer: CVD-safe labels, reveal filter, owned-hex
  selection (completed); **AH-0MWEWYVD7008PPQT** — Navigation: grid columns
  (completed): both pin renderer behaviour this item must preserve.
- **AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP** — Defence report rolled into the hex map (completed):
  source of the attack arrows and the left-hand attack panel now moved into
  `selected-hex`.
- **AH-0MWEZZA4E0081NJ5** — Assault defence report and reset announcement
  (completed): source of the `HANGAR ASSAULT` banner now grouped under
  `last-sortie`.
- **AH-0MWF0CWB7002MG2F** — Special-mission intel (completed): the `★ SPECIAL`
  tile tag whose detail-panel block lives in `selected-hex`.
- **AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2** — Win path: bank a fixed post-win bonus (open): owns the
  `winBonusLine` whose presentation Q3 decides.
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** — Text on hex map is unreadable (completed): the
  legibility baseline this item must not regress.

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** – Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed)
- **AH-0MTGBPRYC000QIHU** – Player has no audio (completed)
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** – Text on hex map is unreadable (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: clearly, create, easily, group, hex, hexmap, identify, information, logical, lot, make, map, much, page, presented, sections, sense, there
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: clearly, create, distinguishable, group, hex, hexmap, lot, make, map, much, page, sections, there
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: create, group, hex, hexmap, logical, lot, make, map, much, page, presented, there

Keyword false positive: `AH-0MTGBPRYC000QIHU` (audio) matched on generic words
(`make`, `there`) and is not related to this item.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Clutter inversion.** More framing can add more visual noise than it removes;
  mitigation: a small fixed section count (4 + footer by default), one heading
  style, and the non-overlap/fit assertions as the guard.
- **Text reflow collisions.** Wrapped draw names and long assault arithmetic are
  the strings that collide at 960×540; mitigation: wrap widths inside each
  section rect plus the "no body text overdraws a tile" assertion.
- **Parity drift.** A scene-local tweak would break gym↔game parity; mitigation:
  all layout in `hexMap.ts`, with the existing equivalence assertions kept.
- **Test churn on positions.** Several suites assert coordinates indirectly;
  mitigation: pin sections structurally (`sections` registry) rather than by
  literal pixel offsets, and update only position-only assertions.
- **Scope creep** into a full visual redesign, new fonts, or tabbed navigation;
  such opportunities are recorded as new linked work items, not absorbed here.
- **Assumption:** headings are monospace text in the existing style (no new
  assets); **assumption:** the attract/demo traversal gains no new state, because
  every section is read-only like today's panels.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (ANSWERED, producer chose (a)) — How should the sections be delineated?**
  (a) Bordered, headed panels in fixed columns — every section has a frame, a
  heading and a bounded rect (recommended).
  (b) Headed bands with separator rules only — headings plus horizontal rules,
  no boxes, more breathing space over the map background.
  (c) Collapsible/tabbed sections — only one section expanded at a time, cutting
  on-screen text but adding interaction state and hidden information.
  **Recommended:** (a) — a frame per section is the most unambiguous
  distinction, needs no new interaction, and is directly assertable (rect +
  heading + non-overlap) by the existing scene/renderer tests.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (a)** bordered, headed panels in fixed
  columns. Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q2 (ANSWERED, producer chose (b)) — Which grouping taxonomy should the map use?**
  (a) Six sections: WAR STATUS, LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX, ATTACK,
  CONTROLS/LEGEND.
  (b) Four sections plus a footer: WAR STATUS, LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX
  (intel **and** its attack row together), CONTROLS/LEGEND (recommended).
  (c) Keep today's regions and only add headings/separators to each.
  **Recommended:** (b) — it separates the three genuinely unlike kinds of
  information (war state, transient news, focused-hex detail) while keeping one
  hex's intel and attack row together, and it avoids the extra section that
  option (a) spends on material that is about the same focused hex.
  Research: the inventory in *Problem statement* comes from
  `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`; the attack panel and the detail panel are both
  keyed by the focused hex (`model.attackDetails` / `displayedHexKey`), which is
  what makes (b) coherent.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (b)** four sections plus a controls footer,
  with the focused hex's intel and its attack row in one `selected-hex` section.
  Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q3 (ANSWERED, producer chose (a)) — Should the banked win-bonus line be
  rendered as part of this item?**
  (a) Yes — render `model.winBonusLine` (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`) inside
  LAST SORTIE (recommended).
  (b) No — leave it query-only and record it as deliberately out of scope.
  (c) Remove the unused line/model field entirely.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the line already exists and is tested through the query
  seam; without it the "what just happened" section silently omits a reward the
  player just earned, and it is a one-line addition to a section this item is
  already building.
  Research: `winBonusLine` is produced by `defenceReport.ts` and republished by
  `hexIntel.ts`; `hexMap.ts` never draws it and `HexMapScene.getWinBonusLine()`
  is its only reader.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (a)** render `model.winBonusLine` inside
  `last-sortie`. Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q4 (recorded, not blocking) — Is a repo/gym search needed for the selected-hex
  line titles?** Answered by inspection of AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK: the titles
  (`ID:`, `STATE:`, `BOSS:`, `STRENGTHS:`, …) are shipped and are treated as a
  fixed input here. Source: work item description + `hexIntel.ts` constants.

# Procedurally generated Hex Map

## Problem statement

The hex ring's **shape** is already generated at runtime from the shared `6 × n`
geometry, but its **content** — boss identity, strengths/weaknesses, the granted
weapon or upgrade, base aggression and the optional variety axes — is
hand-authored data for rings 1 and 2 only, so the war stops where that table
ends. The producer has decided that **every ring should be procedurally
generated from the war's seeded RNG**: the same `(seed, ringIndex)` always yields
the same ring, and the frontier has no authored ceiling.

## Users

- **Player** — "Every war's map is generated from its seed, the frontier never
  stops at ring 2, and the same seed replays the same map."
- **Designer** — "I no longer author a table per ring, and the generator honours
  the shipped ring rules so procedural rings stay balanced and readable."
- **Test/agent** — "The generated ring is a pure function of `(seed, ringIndex)`,
  so I can assert determinism and run it headlessly in the gym with game
  parity."

## Producer decisions (recorded this intake)

- **Q1 = B — all rings procedural.** Rings 1 and 2 are generated from the seed
  like every other ring; `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and the CSV seeds are retired as
  the runtime content source.
- **Q2 = A — pure function of `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`, generated on
  demand.** Only the existing `HexState` is persisted; stored rings are never
  regenerated.
- **Q3 = A — cycle real catalogue grants with level scaling.** Larger rings
  repeat catalogue entries and each repeat raises an upgrade/weapon level
  (capped).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Generated ring content is a **pure, deterministic function of
  `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`**: the same seed/ring yields identical hexes (ids,
  coordinates, boss, strengths/weaknesses, grant, base aggression and variety
  axes), and at least two distinct seeds yield materially different rings.
- The authored runtime table `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and the `hex-ring-1.csv` /
  `hex-ring-2.csv` seeds are **retired as the runtime content source** (no scene
  or runtime path imports authored ring content; the CSV parity test is removed
  or replaced), and rings 1 and 2 generate from the seed like every other ring.
- Every generated ring satisfies the shipped design invariants, validated
  loudly rather than repaired: exactly one weapon hex and it is the ring's
  hardest, one special-mission hex granting a hull, at least one beatable hex,
  unique ids and coordinates, and the aggression band/budget rules.
- **Grant economy:** the generator prefers unowned catalogue entries; when a
  ring exhausts them it cycles level-capable entries and each repeat raises the
  weapon/power-up level (capped at `MAX_LEVEL`), while unlevellable repeats
  (hull/modifier) bank a mineral payout; every granted hex resolves to a real
  effect (never a silent no-op).
- **Existing saves remain playable and unchanged**: a stored ring (full or
  partial) is never regenerated or discarded; a fresh/empty ring generates from
  the seed; defensive parse and migration behaviour is covered by tests.
- Unit, property and integration tests cover determinism, distinct-seed
  variety, invariant enforcement across many seeds and large ring indices, the
  grant-economy rule, and the save/load round-trip; `GymHexWar` renders the same
  generated model as the game.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can push the frontier indefinitely: every war's hex map is generated
from its seed rather than stopping where hand-authored content ends.

## Constraints

- **One seeded stream.** Generation draws from the shipped seeded RNG
  (`createSeededRng` / `createHangarWarRng`, `normaliseSeed`) — no `Math.random`
  in content decisions. Draws must be derived per `(seed, ringIndex)` (and per
  hex) so a change in one ring cannot shift another ring's map.
- **Pure and headless.** The generator lives in the pure core
  (`src/core/hangarWar/`) with no Phaser, storage or scene dependency, so the
  map scene and `GymHexWar` share exactly one code path (gym↔game parity).
- **Preserve the published map.** The known-ahead intel promise (boss,
  strengths/weaknesses, aggression, grant) and the `6 × n` shape are unchanged;
  only *where content comes from* changes.
- **Finite grant vocabulary.** The hangar catalogue holds roughly 12–14 entries
  (hulls, weapons, modifiers, defence-skill), while ring 3 needs 18 distinct
  grants and ring *n* needs `6 × n` — so the level-scaling repeat rule (Q3 = A)
  is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
- **Deterministic identity.** Generated boss identities and hex ids must be
  stable for a seed and traceable in telemetry; hex ids must stay unique within
  the ring and stable across reloads.
- **No new combat implementations.** Personalities resolve through the existing
  bounded vocabularies (`HEX_PERSONALITY_IDS`, `HEX_LANDMARK_IDS`) and shared
  mechanics; generation only assigns them (at most one weapon hex and one
  special mission per ring).
- Aggression stays a whole number in `[0, 9]`; the frontier budget and
  beatable-hex invariants are preserved.

## Existing state

- **Shape generated, content authored.** `ringCoordinates` / `ringSize` compute
  the `6 × n` geometry; `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`)
  authors rings 1 (6 hexes) and 2 (12 hexes). `hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv`
  mirror that table and a parity test fails if they drift.
- **No shipped ring 3.** The only ring-3 content is test fixture data
  (`VARIETY_RING_DEFINITIONS` in
  `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`); `aggressionScenarios.ts`
  already synthesises a deterministic placeholder shape for "ring 3+" in the
  harness — precedent, not shipping code.
- **Materialisation** goes through `materialiseRing` / `openNextRing`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`), which call `createRingState` and leave
  the ring unchanged when an authored successor is missing, so a war stalls at
  the last authored ring.
- **Seeded RNG and seed plumbing exist.** The payload carries a normalised
  `seed` (set from the run seed when a war starts); `createHangarWarRng` exposes
  `next`/`nextInt`/`pick` over the shipped mulberry32 stream, and
  `specialRotationSeed` demonstrates per-index stream mixing.
- **Precedent for generation modes.** AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT shipped per-wave
  `curve` / `fixed` / `dynamic` modes (`dynamic` = regenerated at runtime, seeded
  from the run RNG, reproducible per seed) — the project already has the
  vocabulary for seeded content.
- **The original intake premise was half right:** geometry is runtime-generated,
  content was build-time authored data.

## Desired change

Replace the authored ring-content source with a seeded generator used by **all**
rings. The generator produces a complete, valid `HexRingDefinition`-shaped ring
for any ring index from `(seed, ringIndex)` using the shared RNG and the shipped
catalogues/vocabularies, and flows through the existing materialisation, intel,
map and capture seams. Definition lookup by hex id must be derivable from the
same seed, and repeated catalogue grants must level up rather than no-op.

## **Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — add the seeded ring-content generator; keep
  `validateRingDefinitions` / `generateRing` pure and reuse them.
- `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` — add a per-ring/per-hex derived stream (mirroring
  `specialRotationSeed`); do not add a second generator.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — retire the authored runtime table; keep only
  catalogue/vocabulary exports the generator draws from.
- `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv`, `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv`,
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` — retire the seed/parity pair.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `materialiseRing` / `openNextRing` and
  grant application (`withGrantedEntry`) generate on demand and apply the
  level-scaling repeat rule.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/specialMission.ts` —
  definition lookup by id and the default definitions source consult the
  generator.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts`, `hexDifficulty.ts`, `hexDefence.ts` — the
  profile, aggression band and budget rules the generator must satisfy.
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`, `src/utils/weapons.ts` — the grant pool and the
  level caps (`MAX_LEVEL`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — remove the
  authored default and verify one rendered code path.
- Fixtures/tests: `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`,
  `aggressionScenarios.ts`, `hexVarietyDocs.test.ts`, gym/doc parity tests.
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and module comments.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXC9KG008G80Y** — Hex ring model, generator and ring 1/2 definitions
  (completed). Origin of `hexRing.ts`, `validateRingDefinitions` and the authored
  rings; its producer decision chose authored content, which this item now
  reverses by producer decision (Q1 = B).
- **AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT** — Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed,
  hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration (completed). Closest
  precedent: a `dynamic` mode regenerated at runtime from the run RNG,
  reproducible per seed.
- **AH-0MWEW4ANW009GGX7** — Hex variety data vocabulary, fixtures and loud
  validation (completed). Defines the personality/contract/landmark vocabularies
  the generator assigns.
- **AH-0MWB9V9Q3004HD2P** — HexMap aggression increases too quickly (completed).
  The aggression budget/band rules procedural rings must honour.
- **AH-0MWJ51KUS005WQK6**, **AH-0MWF0CTQB001XFE1** — special-mission hexes;
  **AH-0MWEW5I1F006CLCH** — ring landmarks. The invariants the generator must
  preserve.
- **AH-0MWHWF5D4000J0RB** — Held-hex UPGRADE DEFENCES map action (blocked,
  tangential): consumes the map read model; generated rings must not regress it.
- **AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5** — Rebalance ring 2's grind budget (open, tangential):
  generated aggression must not reintroduce the grind problem it tracks.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Blast radius (main risk).** Retiring the authored table and CSV seeds reaches
  many tests, fixtures, scenes and docs that import `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`.
  Planning should decompose this as an epic into: generator, retirement/migration,
  definition-lookup wiring, grant level-scaling, save compatibility, and
  tests/docs.
- **Determinism contract.** Adding a field or changing a draw order changes every
  seed's map. Treat the draw sequence as a versioned contract and pin it with
  golden tests; scope generation to the pure `(seed, ringIndex)` inputs.
- **Tutorial variance.** Ring 1 is now seed-dependent: every war opens on a
  different ring. If the first war must stay a fixed tutorial, that is a separate
  decision; this brief assumes the producer's all-procedural choice stands.
- **Grant-economy detail.** Q3 = A did not specify repeats of entries with no
  level dimension (hull/modifier). Assumption: prefer unowned entries, level up
  level-capable repeats to `MAX_LEVEL`, and bank a mineral payout for
  unlevellable repeats (reusing the shipped banking rule). Confirm or correct.
- **Validation cost.** Decide whether generated rings are validated on every
  materialisation, only in tests/CI, or once per ring open.
- **Save compatibility.** A stored ring must never be regenerated or lost; an
  old/absent payload must parse defensively. Add a migration test.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Turning this into a new-boss / new-mechanic content suite
  would balloon it. Extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items, not
  folded into this one.

## Open questions

None outstanding — Q1–Q3 are answered. The documented assumptions above (grant
repeats for hulls/modifiers, tutorial variance, validation cadence) are recorded
so the producer can correct them without blocking the plan.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Which rings become procedural, and does the authored content stay?**
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **B — all rings procedural**, including
  rings 1–2; retire `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and the CSV seeds and regenerate
  rings 1–2 from a seed too. Evidence: options recorded in comment
  `AH-C0MWLAGDNN006KLTX`; research inspected
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`, `src/data/hex-ring-*.csv` and
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts`.
- **Q2 — How is a generated ring reproduced and stored?**
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — pure function of
  `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`, generated on demand**; persist only the existing
  `HexState`, no schema migration. Evidence: comment `AH-C0MWLAGECE008CFOM`;
  research inspected `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` (`materialiseRing`),
  `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` (`HangarWarPayload.seed`) and
  `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts`.
- **Q3 — How should generated rings source grants once the catalogue runs out?**
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — cycle real catalogue grants with
  level scaling**; repeats raise an upgrade/weapon level (capped). Evidence:
  comment `AH-C0MWLAGEWP002U2ZA`; research counted ~12–14 catalogue entries in
  `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` against ring 3's 18 required grants, and
  confirmed `withGrantedEntry` currently only adds an owned id (no level raise).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXC9KG008G80Y** – Hex ring model, generator and ring 1/2 definitions (completed)
- **AH-0MWJ4ZDXO007VDJS** – Author shipped hex variety content on ring 1 (one landmark and one contract) (completed)
- **AH-0MVXSHAS100010S0** – Rush push into the next ring is playable (AC8 gap) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mujsuqd8003fsut, 0mwfdqcfv007bze5, 0mwj51kus005wqk6, absent, acceptance (+453 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mujsuqd8003fsut, 0mwfdqcfv007bze5, 0mwj51kus005wqk6, absent, acceptance (+428 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mujsuqd8003fsut, absent, acceptance, action, add (+357 more)
