# Bot selection of upgrades are slower

## Problem statement

When the attract/demo bot is presented with the hold-full upgrade selection
overlay it picks an option after only **900 ms** (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`),
so a viewer has no real chance to read the three offers before the bot has
already chosen — and once it chooses, the choice screen is torn down and only
the 3-2-1 countdown numeral remains, so nothing on screen says **which** item
the bot took. The bot's upgrade picks should dwell long enough to be watched
and should be visible on the countdown.

## Users

- **Attract/demo viewer** (the player watching the menu's 👁 Watch Demo
  attract run, or an idle-menu session): *"As a viewer of attract mode, I want
  to see the bot's upgrade options for a couple of seconds and then see which
  one it picked while the countdown plays, so the demo reads as a deliberate
  choice rather than an instant flicker."*
- **Player (human selection, incidental):** *"As a player, once I choose an
  upgrade I want to be reminded which one I took while the 3-2-1 countdown
  runs."* — the shared overlay tears its choice UI down on selection, so the
  chosen title is the only record during the countdown.
- **Designer / producer:** *"As a designer, I want the bot's overlay dwell to
  be one named, tunable constant so I can pace the demo without hunting magic
  numbers."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **Bot dwell is 2.5 s.** In demo/attract mode the hold-full upgrade
  selection overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`) auto-selects only after a **2500 ms**
  pause, sourced from one named constant (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` in
  `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`, raised from 900); the bot therefore visibly shows
  the offered upgrades before choosing. Normal (non-demo) play still waits for a
  real pointer/keyboard selection and never auto-selects.
- AC2 — **Selected title under the countdown.** From the moment an option is
  selected until the countdown completes, the overlay renders the **chosen
  option's title** (its catalogue name, e.g. `Spread Shot Lv.3`) beneath the
  large 3-2-1 countdown numeral, and the title text is **destroyed** when the
  countdown finishes and the overlay closes — no title text, text object or
  tween outlives the overlay, and a fresh hold-full starts with no stale title.
- AC3 — **Countdown and resume are unchanged.** The selection still drives the
  existing beat-locked 3-2-1 countdown (2250 ms at the default 80 BPM) with its
  rising cue, the reduced-volume ghost fire still runs underneath, and the
  choice is still applied on the beat after "1" with the launcher's beat clock
  re-based. The title is purely additive presentation and never delays or
  alters selection, application or resume timing.
- AC4 — **Scope contained.** The mini-boss reward wheel's demo auto-spin delay
  is **not** changed by AC1 (it keeps its current separate delay/constant), and
  no other surface's timing changes; every gym that launches the shared overlay
  keeps its existing behaviour (no `autoSelectMs` passed) apart from gaining the
  title readout.
- AC5 — **Tests.** Unit tests in `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`
  cover: the chosen title is exposed and rendered while the countdown runs, and
  is gone (`null`) after the countdown completes; a manual selection shows its
  own title; the constant-pinned bot dwell is asserted (auto-select does not
  fire before 2500 ms and does fire after it). The demo integration test
  (`src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`) still asserts the
  selection → countdown → resume path and asserts the selected title is visible
  during the countdown. All existing overlay, gym-parity and countdown tests
  stay green.
- AC6 — **Docs.** `README.md` (attract/demo mode section) and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 auto-select bullet and §4.5
  beat-locked-countdown bullet) are updated to state the **2.5 s** bot dwell
  and the selected title shown under the countdown (and removed with it).
- AC7 — **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.**
- AC8 — **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A viewer of the attract-mode demo now gets a clear 2.5-second look at the bot's
three upgrade offers and can see exactly which one it took while the countdown
plays, instead of a near-instant pick that left no trace of the choice.

## Constraints

- Demo-only for the dwell: normal play must not gain any auto-selection
  (existing AC5 of AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB must stay true).
- Tunables live in one shared place (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`), never as
  scattered magic numbers.
- The overlay keeps its single `onSelect` contract; it must not reach back into
  `PlayScene` by scene key.
- The countdown stays beat-derived (`createHoldFullCountdown` /
  `beatPeriodMs`), never a hard-coded 2250 ms.
- Headless test harnesses collapse text metrics to 0, so any title layout must
  keep a measurable fallback (mirroring the existing `CHOICE_*_LINE_HEIGHT`
  constants) and stay inside the 960 × 720 playfield.
- The overlay is shared by `PlayScene`, `HexMapScene`, `GymFormationScene`,
  `GymWeaponLeveling` and `GymPowerUpLeveling`; the title addition must keep
  gym↔game parity (no per-scene copies).

## Existing state

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` exports `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS = 900` — the
  demo dwell used for the hold-full choice auto-select, the mini-boss
  hold-full-style fallback choice, **and** the mini-boss wheel auto-spin
  (`PlayScene.openMiniBossReward` → `autoSpinMs`).
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (`init` → `autoSelectMs` /
  `autoSelectIndex`, `create` → `this.time.delayedCall`) auto-selects on the
  demo path. `select(index)` records the pending selection, tears down the
  whole choice UI (backdrop, heading, option labels/descriptions/details, the
  `★ New` badges, the `YOUR UPGRADES` panel, the keydown handler) and draws the
  large countdown numeral at `COUNTDOWN_Y = 270` (96 px, neon cyan).
  `completeSelection()` destroys the numeral, invokes `onSelect` and stops the
  scene. Public accessors already exist: `getCountdownText()`,
  `isCountdownActive()`, `isChoiceScreenVisible()`, `getOverlayElapsedMs()`.
- `src/scenes/core/holdFullCountdown.ts` owns the pure 3-2-1 scheduler
  (`HOLD_FULL_COUNTDOWN_COUNTS = 3`, `HOLD_FULL_COUNTDOWN_DURATION_MS`).
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` uses its own `demoDwellMs ?? HANGAR_WAR_TRAVERSAL_DWELL_MS`
  for demo reward overlays, so it does not depend on the bot choice constant.
- Docs pin the current 900 ms pace: `README.md` (attract/demo paragraph) and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 ("**900 ms**") and §4.5 (countdown tears
  the choice screen down, "leaving only the countdown numeral").
- Tests reference the constant symbolically (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`), so
  a value change flows through `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` and
  `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` waits without hard-coded numbers.

## Desired change

1. Raise the demo dwell to 2500 ms (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`), keeping the
   mini-boss wheel's demo spin delay at its current pace via a separate constant
   so only the upgrade-selection pause slows.
2. In `MineralChoiceScene`, render the chosen option's title beneath the
   countdown numeral when a selection starts the countdown, expose it for tests
   (e.g. `getCountdownTitle()`), and destroy it alongside the numeral in
   `completeSelection()` (and defensively on shutdown).
3. Update the overlay's module doc comment, README and GDD to describe the
   2.5 s bot dwell and the title-under-countdown readout.
4. Cover the above with unit tests and keep the demo integration and gym-parity
   suites green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — raise `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` to 2500 and
  (if the wheel is scoped out) add a separate demo-spin delay constant; update
  the doc comment.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — new countdown-title text object + layout
  constant, title creation in `select()`, destruction in `completeSelection()`
  and shutdown, `getCountdownTitle()` accessor, module doc comment.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — hold-full/mini-boss-fallback `autoSelectMs` wiring
  and the wheel `autoSpinMs` constant separation (comments mention the new
  pace).
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — title-visible/title-cleared
  and 2500 ms dwell tests.
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` — assert the selected title under
  the countdown on the demo path.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — only where the wheel/choice delay is asserted.
- `README.md` — attract/demo paragraph: 2.5 s dwell + selected title.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 auto-select bullet, §4.5 countdown
  bullet.

## Related work

- AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB — *Demo bot: human-like input limits and complete the
  hold-full upgrade choice* (completed): introduced the demo auto-select and
  `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`.
- AH-0MV55OBKS006TL4N — *Demo/attract auto-select routes through the countdown*
  (completed): the bot's auto-select must drive the same selection → 3-2-1 →
  on-beat resume path.
- AH-0MV55OAQT004NMSN — *Beat-locked 3-2-1 countdown and on-beat resume*
  (completed): owns the countdown scheduler and the "numeral only" teardown this
  item extends with the chosen title.
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F — *AI bot does not know how to select upgrade in
  mini-boss reward screen* (completed): the mini-boss reward auto-select and
  wheel spin sharing the same demo delay.
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — *Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the
  ship's hold and grant a power-up choice* (completed): the hold-full overlay
  itself.
- AH-0MV722WJS0075UTZ — countdown teardown of the choice UI (the behaviour the
  title readout complements).
- AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4 / AH-0MW3MLV2V001NWBR — the retired Extra Life
  auto-select preference; the auto-select always takes option 0 today.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z** – Some power-ups appear to do nothing (completed)
- **AH-0MV55OBKS006TL4N** – Demo/attract auto-select routes through the
  countdown (completed)
- **AH-0MVD20MYX0028JFL** – Close coverage gap: AC2 upgrade choices simulated
  (completed)

### Potentially related docs

- `README.md` (attract/demo mode paragraph) — documents the current 900 ms
  auto-select and the countdown/resume cadence.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (bot) and §4.5 (hold-full overlay) —
  the two canonical descriptions of this behaviour.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — demo capture expectations that exercise the
  overlay.

## Assumptions and decisions for producer confirmation

- **A1 — Dwell scope.** The 2.5 s pause applies to the **upgrade selection
  overlay** only (hold-full choice, and the hold-full-style mini-boss
  fallback, which reuse `MineralChoiceScene`). The **mini-boss reward wheel**
  keeps its current demo auto-spin pace (split into its own constant), because
  the item describes an upgrade *selection* screen; the wheel has no selection
  and no titled options. *If the producer wants every bot reward overlay
  slowed to 2.5 s, AC4 is simply dropped and the wheel keeps the shared
  constant.*
- **A2 — Title scope.** The chosen title is shown for **every** selection on the
  shared overlay (bot auto-select and human), not bot-only: the choice UI is
  torn down for both, so the readout is equally useful and there is no penalty
  in normal play. *If bot-only is wanted, gate the title on the demo flag.*
- **A3 — Title copy.** The "title" is the option's catalogue `name` (e.g.
  `Spread Shot Lv.3`), i.e. the same text the option label carried (without the
  `1.` prefix), not the change summary or description.
- **A4 — Countdown timing unchanged.** The 3-2-1 countdown stays three beats
  (2250 ms at 80 BPM) and still applies the choice on the beat after "1".
- **A5 — Title lifetime.** The title clears when the countdown completes (the
  overlay closes); it is not carried into gameplay or the HUD.

## Risks

- **Scope creep** — "make the demo's pacing nicer" invites unrelated overlay
  restyling; anything beyond the dwell + title readout becomes a linked
  follow-up item, not this item.
- **Timing fragility** — lengthening the dwell changes total overlay duration
  (2500 + 2250 ms); integration tests that wait on constants remain valid, but
  any test with a hard-coded wait must move to `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`
  arithmetic.
- **Shared overlay regression** — the title must be torn down with the numeral
  in every exit path (completion, scene shutdown, scene restart) or a stale
  text object can leak between hold-fulls.
- **Wheel coupling** — `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` currently feeds the
  wheel's `autoSpinMs`; splitting it is the only way to keep AC4 true, so the
  split must be explicit and documented.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the 2.5 s pause apply to every bot reward overlay (hold-full
  choice, mini-boss wheel spin, hex-map demo reward overlays) or only the
  upgrade selection screen?"
  — Answer (agent, assumption A1, producer confirmation invited): only the
  upgrade selection overlay; the mini-boss wheel keeps its current delay via a
  separate constant. Source: work-item seed description ("the upgrade selection
  screen", "select whichever one they want") + repo inspection of
  `PlayScene.openMineralChoice` / `openMiniBossReward` / `HexMapScene`.
- Q: "Should the chosen title appear under the countdown for human selections
  too, or only for the bot?"
  — Answer (agent, assumption A2, producer confirmation invited): every
  selection on the shared overlay, because `select()` tears down the choice UI
  for both paths so the readout costs normal play nothing. Source: repo
  inspection of `MineralChoiceScene.select()` / `completeSelection()`.
- Q: "What is the 'title' — the option name, its change summary, or its
  description?"
  — Answer (agent, assumption A3): the catalogue option `name` (e.g.
  `Spread Shot Lv.3`), matching the label the option row showed. Source: seed
  wording "selected item's title" + `ChoiceOption` shape in
  `src/powerups/choice.ts`.
- Q: "Does the 3-2-1 countdown itself change length?"
  — Answer (agent, assumption A4): no — it stays beat-locked at three counts
  (2250 ms at the default 80 BPM) with the choice applied on the beat after
  "1". Source: `src/scenes/core/holdFullCountdown.ts` and
  AH-0MV55OAQT004NMSN.
- Q: "Which docs pin the current 900 ms pace?"
  — Answer (agent research): `README.md` attract/demo paragraph and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 ("**900 ms**") and §4.5 (countdown
  "leaving only the countdown numeral"). Both need updating.

**Phase 1 of 5 — test-first.** Parent: AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ (AC2, AC3, AC14).

## Goal

Write the **failing** tests that pin the matchup rule's contract and the authoring
normalisation/validation, before any implementation lands. This is the red half
of the tracer bullet for the pure core slice.

## Context

The authored `strengths`/`weaknesses` lists are inert display text today.
Parent decision Q4 = (a): the authored lists stay authoritative, but the
resolver's input must be shaped as an **injectable verdict lookup for a weapon
id** so a damage-type-derived lookup can land later behind the same seam.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexMatchup.test.ts` exists and pins `resolveHexMatchup(weaponId, lookup)` returning `'effective' | 'neutral' | 'resisted'` for a supplied lookup, and `'neutral'` for an unknown weapon id, `null`, `undefined`, and an unauthored hex.
- A test supplies a **synthetic** verdict lookup containing no authored data and no import from `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`, proving the rule is decoupled from the lists' storage (AC14).
- A test pins the resisted-rate **tie rule** through a pure ledger: exactly one hit point per two connected shots, the credit accruing to the second shot of each pair, keyed per target and per weapon, and reset on target death.
- Tests pin **both** load-time validation failure modes — an authored id resolving to no catalogue weapon, and a weapon appearing in **both** lists of the same hex — each throwing with the hex id and offending entry named.
- A shipped-data test asserts every authored `strengths`/`weaknesses` entry normalises to a catalogue weapon id (`waveLaser` → `wave_laser`) and validates clean, so the guard breaks nothing shipped today.
- Every new test is **red** against the current tree and names the missing export/behaviour in its failure.


### Parent acceptance-criteria trace

- (AC2) A **pure, headless** matchup resolver lives in `src/core/hangarWar/` and is the only place the advantage/handicap is decided; unit-tested for `effective` / `neutral` / `resisted`, for an **unknown weapon id** (neutral, total) and for an **unauthored hex** (neutral). Its input is a **verdict lookup for a weapon id**, not a direct scan of the authored lists.

# Saved ship configurations: re-purchase and equip a known build in one action

## Problem statement

When a hex battle ends, the deployed ship is consumed (AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF) and the player must rebuild from salvage, so re-purchasing and re-equipping a known build is repeated busywork. Saved ship configurations let the player store a named build once and re-apply it — purchase plus equip every part — in a single action, then fly.

## Users

- **Primary — the player** who repeatedly flies the same preferred build through the hex war and re-fits it after each sortie.
- **Secondary — the balance/progression owner**, because reducing re-fit friction makes the post-battle economy treadmill tolerable.

Example user stories:

- As a player, I want to save my preferred build by name, so I don't have to remember which hull, weapons and modifiers I fly.
- As a player, I want to select a saved build from a drop-down and have every part purchased and equipped in one action, so re-fitting after a battle takes one click instead of a dozen.
- As a player, I want a saved build I cannot currently afford to tell me exactly what is missing (which entries/minerals/cores), so I know what to earn before I try again.
- As a player, I want to rename or delete saved builds, so the list stays useful as my builds evolve.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Save a named build.** The hangar can capture the currently equipped ship configuration as a named saved build: the equipped hull (`activeHull`), the equipped starting weapons (`activeLoadout.startingWeapons`), the equipped modifiers (`activeLoadout.modifiers`), and the permanent levels that configuration relies on (`hangar.weaponLevels` / `hangar.powerUpLevels` rows for those kinds).
- **One-action purchase and equip.** A drop-down on the hangar screen lists saved builds; selecting one **purchases and equips every upgrade the build needs in one action** — the hull becomes `activeHull`, starting weapons join `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, modifiers join `activeLoadout.modifiers`, and any missing permanent levels are bought — through the existing pure economy/payload updaters, never scene-only logic.
- **Affordable builds apply atomically; unaffordable builds report the shortfall.** A build whose combined salvage cost the player cannot currently afford must report the exact shortfall (which entries, minerals and/or cores are missing) and apply **nothing** — neither partial purchase nor partial equip, and no currency spent.
- **Saved builds can be saved, renamed and deleted.** The hangar surface supports creating a saved build from the current configuration, renaming an existing one, and deleting one, and the list is persisted in the hangar-war payload. **Saved builds survive a war reset** (producer decision): `restartHangarWar` preserves the saved-build list alongside `bestScore`, because saved configurations are a "what you own" meta-layer rather than war progress.
- **Saved builds are unbounded in number, with a delete affordance.** There is no cap on how many saved builds a player may hold (producer decision), so the drop-down list plus the save/rename/delete surface is the only management mechanism — deleting a build must be reachable for every entry.
- **A saved build referencing a now-unavailable entry never breaks.** Selecting a saved build whose parts are not in the catalogue (or are ring-gated) reports the same shortfall/refusal path rather than throwing or silently applying a partial build; the economy's `owned → gated → unaffordable` precedence is respected.
- **Automated tests cover the feature through the pure core and the scene seam (gym↔game parity).** Saving captures the exact equipped set plus level rows; selecting an affordable build purchases and equips atomically; an unaffordable build reports every missing item/currency and applies nothing; rename/delete round-trip (deletion reachable for every saved build); a saved build missing a catalogue entry refuses safely; `restartHangarWar` keeps the saved-build list while wiping unlocks/levels/loadout; and the payload round-trips through `hangarWarStore` without a schema-version bump (the shape is additive).
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

After a battle you pick your saved build from the hangar drop-down and, if you can afford it, the whole ship is re-purchased and re-equipped in one action — re-fitting becomes one click instead of repeated busywork.

## Constraints

- **Pure core, scene seam.** Purchase, equip and level arithmetic live in the pure economy/payload updaters; the screen and scene only present and persist, so gym↔game parity holds (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`).
- **Atomic apply.** A build applies fully or not at all; no partial purchase, no partial equip, no spend on a refused build.
- **Additive payload field.** Saved builds are a new optional field on the hangar payload, migrated by field presence without a schema-version bump (the established pattern for `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` / `frontierTick`), and omitted on write when empty so a save round-trips byte-for-byte.
- **War-reset interaction.** `restartHangarWar` currently calls `createDefaultPayload`, which resets the entire hangar to starters (all unlocks, levels and loadout). The producer decided **saved builds survive a reset**, so `restartHangarWar` must thread `savedBuilds` through beside `bestScore` (other hangar state stays at the reset default).
- **One payload write.** Applying a build persists through the existing `saveHangarWarPayload`; demo/attract runs must never overwrite the player's war (existing demo guard).
- **No soft-lock.** A saved build must never leave the player with no deployable ship; the free starter hull/weapon rules are unchanged.
- **Economy precedence preserved.** A build's parts are validated with the existing `owned → gated → unaffordable` rule; auto-enable on purchase (AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR) is the per-part primitive this feature composes, not a re-implementation.
- **Scope creep risk.** A full loadout-preset/sharing system, cross-device sync, or balance tuning of prices is out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Existing state

- `HangarState` (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) holds `activeHull`, `activeLoadout` (starting weapons + modifiers), `unlockedHulls`/`unlockedWeapons`/`ownedModifiers`, and optional `weaponLevels`/`powerUpLevels` rows; it has **no** saved-build field.
- `hangarEconomy.ts` owns the pure purchase rules (`buy`, `canBuy`, `costToUpgrade`, `buyUpgrade`, `equipHull`, `equipLoadout`, `resolveActiveLoadout`) and the `owned → gated → unaffordable` precedence.
- `hangarScreen.ts` exposes pure payload updaters (`purchaseHangarEntry`, `upgradeHangarKind`, `equipHangarHull`, `toggleHangarWeapon`, `restartHangarWar`) and the shared `buildHangarScreenModel`/`renderHangarScreen` used by both `HangarScene` and `GymHangar`.
- `hangarWarStore.ts` parses/normalises the payload (additive fields migrated by presence) and `createDefaultPayload` seeds the starter kit.
- AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR (auto-enable a purchase in the hangar) is the per-part "buying arms it immediately" primitive this feature builds on; AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF is the parent consumption work.

## Desired change

- Add a saved-build contract (name + hull + starting weapons + modifiers + the permanent level rows the build relies on) and an additive `savedBuilds` field on `HangarState`/the payload, parsed and normalised like the other additive fields.
- Add pure helpers to capture the current configuration as a build, and a pure "apply a saved build" reducer that validates affordability and atomically purchases + equips every part (reusing `buy` with `equipOnPurchase` and the level-upgrade path), returning either the new payload or a structured shortfall.
- Surface a drop-down list plus save/rename/delete affordances on the hangar screen, with the unaffordable shortfall rendered like the existing refused-purchase messaging.
- Persist through the single `saveHangarWarPayload` write; confirm the payload round-trips without a schema bump.
- Preserve the saved-build list across `restartHangarWar` (thread `savedBuilds` through beside `bestScore`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **War-reset boundary (resolved).** `restartHangarWar` resets the whole hangar to starters; the producer decided saved builds survive, so thread `savedBuilds` through `restartHangarWar` beside `bestScore`. Test that a reset keeps the saved-build list while wiping unlocks/levels/loadout.
- **Partial-application bugs.** Applying a build touches ownership, loadout and level rows at once. Mitigation: one pure reducer that either returns a complete new payload or a structured shortfall, with a test asserting no currency is spent on refusal.
- **Stale builds.** A saved build may name a ring-gated or removed catalogue entry after a war reset or catalogue change. Mitigation: validate through the economy's `owned → gated → unaffordable` precedence and report the shortfall rather than partially applying.
- **Atomicity vs auto-enable.** AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR auto-enables a *single* purchase; a build is many purchases that must land atomically. Mitigation: compose the per-part primitive inside the build reducer, not the screen.
- **UI list growth.** Saved builds are unbounded by producer decision. Mitigation: the delete affordance keeps the list manageable; render the drop-down with scrolling if it overflows the screen.
- **Scope creep.** A general loadout-preset/sharing system or price/balance tuning could creep in. Mitigation: record extra opportunities as linked work items; keep this item to save/apply/rename/delete + shortfall.
- **Assumptions:** saved builds capture equipped ids plus the level rows they rely on; applying a build validates all parts before spending; demo/attract runs never persist a build application (existing demo guard).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — add `SavedShipBuild` and the additive `savedBuilds?` field on `HangarState`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — pure `buildFromHangar`, `applySavedBuild` (atomic purchase+equip, structured shortfall), reusing `buy`/`buyUpgrade`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — parse/normalise `savedBuilds` by field presence (no version bump), omit when empty.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — pure `saveBuild`/`renameBuild`/`deleteBuild`/`selectBuild` updaters plus screen model rows for the drop-down and management actions; `restartHangarWar` preserves `savedBuilds`.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — wire the updaters and the single persist.
- Tests beside each module plus the `hangarWarFlow` integration test and the gym parity scene.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF** — Completing a hex battle means the equipped hulls/weapons/plugins are reset (parent; defines the consumption this feature re-fits after).
- **AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR** — Auto-enable a purchase in the hangar (the per-part buy-and-arm primitive this feature composes).
- **AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6** — Hangar economy and unlock tree (the purchase/equip rules).
- **AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1** — Hangar screen shared model/renderer (the surface this extends).
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** — Empty-loadout legality (must be preserved).
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D persistence rules), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MT9FRVF00086TO3** – Ship configuration file: load and save values (completed) — a *run-time* ship-stat config file, not the hangar economy; related by name only.
- **AH-0MT9FS3DL0084Z6V** – Gym scene: ship config sliders, save button, half-speed ship (completed) — run-time gym ship config; related by name only.
- **AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T** – Set Asteroids as the default ship control scheme and accept headerless CSV seed format (completed) — unrelated (control scheme / seed format).
- **Repository matches:** `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should a saved build capture permanent levels too, not just the equipped ids?" — Answer (seed context, AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF Q1 follow-on): yes — the build includes "the permanent levels the build relies on", so re-applying it buys the levels as well as the parts. Source: parent item description and producer's Q1 follow-on (save ship configurations, select to quickly purchase the needed upgrades).
- Q: "What should happen when the player cannot afford every part of a saved build?" — Answer (seed context, this item): report the shortfall (which entries/minerals/cores are missing) rather than partially applying or silently failing — apply nothing. Source: item description; consistent with the economy's refused-purchase contract.
- Q: "Do saved builds survive a war reset (RESTART WAR / `restartHangarWar`)?" — Answer (producer): **yes** — saved builds survive a war reset; `restartHangarWar` preserves the saved-build list alongside `bestScore`. Source: interactive reply (producer Q1 = yes), 2026-11-17.
- Q: "Is the drop-down on the existing hangar screen, or a new surface?" — Answer: on the existing hangar screen (`buildHangarScreenModel`/`renderHangarScreen`), so gym parity is automatic. Source: this item description ("A drop-down on the hangar screen"); AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1.
- Q: "Should saved builds be scoped/limited (max count)?" — Answer (producer): **unbounded**, but provide a way to delete them. Source: interactive reply (producer Q2), 2026-11-17.

## Traceability

- Duplicate check performed — searched `saved build configuration hangar`; no existing item covers saved ship configurations. Closest items are the parent consumption work (AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF), the auto-enable primitive (AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR) and the economy/screen items listed above, which this item composes rather than duplicates.

# Owned hexes provide minerals (AH-0MWL8CDGN005878A)

## Problem statement

Holding a hex on the ring currently has no economic payoff between sorties:
the only persistent mineral income is the salvage a run banks at its checkpoint
and the fixed win bonus, so capturing hexes buys safety and loadout grants but
never a stream of minerals. Give each **held** hex a deterministic per-tick
mineral income proportional to its aggression (`10 × aggression` per hex,
summed over the hexes still held after the tick) and bank it into the
persistent hangar balance (`hangar.bankedMinerals`) alongside the existing
salvage, so owning territory compounds into the weapons and upgrades the
player buys.

## Users

- **As a Hangar War player**, I want every hex I hold to pay mineral income each
  between-sortie tick scaled by how hard that hex is to keep, so taking and
  holding high-aggression territory is economically worthwhile and the ring
  reads as an asset, not just a boss list.
- **As a Hangar War player**, I want the income announced when the
  between-sortie report lands, so I can see my holdings paying out rather than
  wondering where the extra minerals came from.
- **As a producer**, I want the income rule to be a single pure, tunable
  arithmetic rule over the ring's held hexes with no saved-field migration, so
  the balance can be retuned by one constant without a schema version bump.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Pure, deterministic income rule.** A new pure rule computes the
  per-tick mineral income as
  `Σ over ring.hexes where held: HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION × aggression`
  (`HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION = 10`, producer Q1). It returns a
  non-negative whole number and consumes **no RNG and no wall clock**. Table
  tests pin the empty ring (`0`), a one-held-hex ring (`10 × aggression`), a
  partially held ring (only held hexes counted), and a fallen hex contributing
  `0`.
- **AC2 — Banked once per between-sortie tick.** One `runFrontierTick` adds the
  AC1 amount to `hangar.bankedMinerals`; a second tick banks again (income is
  per-tick, not one-off), and a demo-mode sortie never persists its income. A
  test proves a single sortie resolves one tick and therefore banks one income
  amount (no double-bank via the win path and `_finishRun`).
- **AC3 — Post-tick snapshot (producer Q2 = b).** Income is computed from the
  ring **after** the tick's aggression redistribution and after the AI attacks
  resolve, counting only hexes still `held` and using their post-tick
  `aggression`. A hex lost during the tick therefore pays nothing for that
  tick. A test drives a tick that loses a held hex and asserts the fallen hex
  contributes `0` while survivors pay `10 × aggression`.
- **AC4 — Tick record and report visibility (producer Q3 = a).**
  `FrontierTickRecord` carries the income (`hexIncome`), and the between-sortie
  report/map renders a `HEX INCOME BANKED: +N MINERALS` line when `N > 0`
  (mirroring the existing `winBonusLine`), with no line when `N = 0`. A test
  asserts the line for a ring with held hexes and its absence for an empty
  ring.
- **AC5 — Gym and headless parity.** `GymHexWar` and the headless evaluation
  arena, which already call `runFrontierTick`, expose the same income in the
  tick record through the shared code path (no gym-local re-derivation), and
  never double-count because a re-render re-runs the pure tick on a retained
  payload. A gym test asserts the record's income matches the game's for the
  same payload.
- **AC6 — Migration and robustness.** No new persisted field is required: a
  save written before this change still ticks, deriving income from its
  current held hexes. Corrupt, negative or non-integer aggression and held
  state normalise safely (`aggression` clamped to a non-negative integer, a
  non-held hex contributes `0`); the banked balance is clamped to a
  non-negative integer on write, and the income never consumes a seeded RNG
  draw (the aggression and attack streams stay byte-identical for the same
  payload/seed/tick).
- **AC7 — Docs and comments.** README (Hangar War / hex map and economy
  sections), the GDD §8.2 economy notes and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
  (Candidate D) describe the income rule and mark the `10 × aggression`
  multiplier a balance knob; the new rule's JSDoc states the formula, the
  post-tick timing decision and the migration behaviour. All related
  documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
  README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC8 — Test suite.** Focused unit tests cover the pure rule, the tick
  integration, the post-tick ordering case, the no-RNG-draw property and the
  report line; full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Holding territory now pays out every between-sortie tick in proportion to each
hex's aggression, so a player's owned hexes visibly fund the weapons and
upgrades they buy instead of only granting a one-off capture reward.

## Constraints

- **Pure arithmetic only.** The design of record
  (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, Candidate D) requires that between-run
  economy and frontier resolution stay *algorithmic over stored numbers* — no
  simulated economy, no wall clock, no new RNG stream (adding a draw would
  shift the seeded frontier stream and break deterministic replays).
- **Post-tick snapshot (producer Q2 = b).** Income is read from the payload
  *after* redistribution and attacks, so it must be computed at the end of
  `runFrontierTick`, not before.
- **One shared code path.** The game, `GymHexWar` and the headless arena must
  bank/expose income through `runFrontierTick` and one pure rule; no divergent
  copy (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).
- **No schema break.** The payload is field-presence migrated; the income is
  derived from `ring.hexes[].held` and `ring.hexes[].aggression`, which already
  exist, so no new persisted field and no `version` bump.
- **Balance note.** At `10 × aggression`, a fully held ring 1 (aggression
  total 18) pays `180`/tick, which exceeds the `100` win bonus and the measured
  ~24 minerals per deployment. This is the producer's Q1 choice; the multiplier
  is a single tunable constant and any retune is a one-line change (a
  re-baselining follow-up, not folded into this item).

## Existing state

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — `runFrontierTick` is the one
  between-sortie transition: it redistributes aggression, resolves attacks and
  advances `frontierTick`, returning `{ payload, clock, record }`. It does not
  currently touch `hangar.bankedMinerals`. `applyDefence` clears `held` and
  `defender` on a fallen hex but keeps its aggression.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HexState.held` is the ownership flag and
  `HexState.aggression` the per-hex value; `HangarState.bankedMinerals` is the
  persistent balance.
- `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` — `bankSalvage` / `bankWinBonus` bank
  minerals from checkpoint snapshots and the fixed win bonus; the income rule
  is a third, independent source into the same balance.
- `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` — `winBonusLine` is the existing
  announcement pattern (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`) the income line
  mirrors.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_resolveBetweenSortieTick` runs the tick once
  per sortie (the win path resolves it before the capture and `_finishRun`
  reuses `pendingBetweenSortieTick`), so banking is naturally per-sortie.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — calls `runFrontierTick` for the map record.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — Candidate D names a "per-tick arithmetic
  rule over the region's holdings" and the algorithmic-resolution constraint.
- `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` and AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA — the income
  anchor: ~24 minerals mean per ring-1 deployment, ~22.3 per ring-2 grind
  deployment.

## Desired change

1. Add a pure `hexIncome` rule (in `hexDefence.ts` or a small sibling module)
   that sums `HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION × aggression` over the hexes
   still held after the tick, normalising to a non-negative integer and
   consuming no RNG.
2. Call it at the **end** of `runFrontierTick` (after redistribution and
   attacks), adding the result to `next.hangar.bankedMinerals` and exposing it
   on `FrontierTickRecord` as `hexIncome`.
3. Thread the income through the report/map model as a `hexIncomeLine` sibling
   of `winBonusLine`, rendered as `HEX INCOME BANKED: +N MINERALS`.
4. Document the rule and the `10 × aggression` balance knob.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — add the pure income rule and the
  `HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION` constant; apply it at the end of
  `runFrontierTick`; extend `FrontierTickRecord`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.test.ts` — pure-rule table tests, tick banking,
  post-tick ordering, fallen-hex contribution and zero-RNG-draw assertions.
- `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` — `hexIncomeLine` on the report model.
- `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.test.ts` — line present/absent cases.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — carry the income line through the map
  model.
- `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` — reference only; confirm the third
  income source does not disturb the checkpoint watermark.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts` — gym record parity.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md` —
  document the rule and multiplier.
- `src/core/hangarWar/fixtures.ts` — a held-ring fixture if an existing one is
  insufficient.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` (added at plan) — the local
  `FrontierTickRecord` stub factory must gain `hexIncome` for the type to
  compile; its map-overlay assertions cover the threaded line.
- `src/defenceReportRolledInDocs.test.ts` (added at plan) — the existing docs
  guard that pins `WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS` in the GDD; add the income
  line beside it so the docs change cannot silently regress.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA** (completed) — Re-baseline salvage, cores and the
  mini-boss reward value per hex deployment. Supplies the per-deployment income
  anchor (~24 / ~22.3 minerals) against which the new rate is judged.
- **AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2** (open) — Win path: suppress the mini-boss wheel and
  bank a fixed post-win bonus on hex wins. The `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` /
  `winBonusLine` pattern this feature mirrors.
- **AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP** — between-sortie frontier tick (the transition that
  hosts the income).
- **AH-0MVUXC118004B4OX** — salvage banking at checkpoint moments (the other
  persistent mineral source).
- **AH-0MWB9V9Q3004HD2P** — strength-budgeted frontier clock (the tick's
  invariants the income must not perturb).
- **AH-0MWH4F375000X08G / AH-0MWJ4ZDXO007VDJS** — hex variety (landmarks,
  contracts, cache payouts) that a future per-hex yield could build on.
- **AH-0MWL4QCVD007WOAM** (open) — Hex Map Information UX; the natural surface
  for a per-hex income intel line.
- Duplicate check performed: `wl search minerals` and `wl search "owned hex"`
  returned no completed item delivering per-tick income from held hexes, so
  this is net-new work.

## Assumptions

- A1: "each tick" means the existing **between-sortie frontier tick**
  (`runFrontierTick`), not a wall-clock or frame tick — the design of record
  defines the between-run tick as the economy's cadence.
- A2: "owned hexes" means `HexState.held === true` in the current ring; the
  payload stores only the current ring, so income is over that ring.
- A3: Income is minerals only (no cores), matching the win bonus's
  minerals-only rule, because cores are the rarer mini-boss currency.
- A4: The `10 × aggression` multiplier is the producer's Q1 balance choice; it
  is one tunable constant and may be retuned without migration.

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-18)

### Planning decision

**No child decomposition.** This is one cohesive, small (Small effort / Medium
risk) vertical slice: a pure rule plus the one call site that already exists,
the report line that mirrors `winBonusLine`, and the docs. Splitting it into
"tests", "rule", "report", "docs" children would produce horizontal layers
that cannot each be delivered end-to-end, which the skill's vertical-slice rule
forbids. The item is therefore planned as a single implementable unit and the
plan below is the ordering inside it.

### Test-first implementation order

1. **Pure-rule tests** in `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.test.ts`: empty ring
   `0`, one held hex `10 × aggression`, partially held ring (only held hexes),
   a held hex with aggression `0` contributing `0`, and hostile input
   (negative/`NaN`/non-integer aggression) normalising to a non-negative
   whole number. → verify: the new tests fail against the current module.
2. **`hexIncome(hexes)` rule** in `hexDefence.ts` plus
   `HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION = 10`, exported for the report tests and
   documented with the JSDoc AC1/AC3/AC6 require. → verify: step-1 tests pass;
   the rule calls neither `tickRng` nor `Date`.
3. **Tick integration**: call the rule at the **end** of `runFrontierTick`
   (after `redistribution` is applied to the hexes and after every
   `applyDefence`), add it to `next.hangar.bankedMinerals` through the existing
   `toCount`, and publish it on the record as `hexIncome`. Add the tick tests:
   one tick banks once, a second tick banks again, a hex lost this tick pays
   `0` while survivors pay `10 × aggression`, and two ticks over payloads that
   differ only in `bankedMinerals` return identical `deltas`/`attacks` (the
   no-RNG-draw property). → verify: tick tests pass; still one `runFrontierTick`
   result per sortie (AC2).
4. **Report + map line**: `hexIncomeLine` on `DefenceReportModel`, derived from
   `record.hexIncome` (see clarification C1), threaded through
   `HexMapAttackOverlay` in `hexIntel.ts` and its `QUIET_TICK_RECORD`/
   `FrontierTickRecord` stubs (`hexIncome: 0`). Tests assert the line for a
   held ring and its absence for an empty one, and that the gym's record income
   equals the game's for the same payload. → verify: report, intel and gym
   suites pass.
5. **Docs**: README (Hangar War / hex map-and-economy sections), GDD §8.2
   (`#### The hangar and its economy`, and the `Measured per-deployment income`
   note that should point at the new stream), `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
   Candidate D; mark `10 × aggression` a balance knob; extend
   `src/defenceReportRolledInDocs.test.ts`. → verify: docs guard tests pass.

### Implementation clarifications (review-stage findings)

- **C1 — `hexIncomeLine` reads the record, not a new option.** `winBonusMinerals`
  is a `BuildDefenceReportOptions` field because the win bonus is banked by the
  *capture* path, outside the tick. Income is banked *inside* the tick, so it
  already travels on `FrontierTickRecord`: `buildDefenceReport` must derive
  `hexIncomeLine` from `toCount(record.hexIncome)` and add **no** new option.
  That keeps gym↔game parity automatic (AC5) and leaves `hexIntel`'s
  `winBonusMinerals` plumbing untouched.
- **C2 — demo mode is already handled.** `PlayScene._saveHangarWarPayload`
  returns before `saveHangarWarPayload` when `this.demoMode` is true, so a demo
  sortie's banked income is never persisted. No demo-specific branch belongs in
  the income rule; AC2's demo clause is satisfied by asserting the payload was
  not persisted, not by branching in `runFrontierTick`.
- **C3 — the win path resolves one tick.** `_resolveHangarWarCapture` stores
  `pendingBetweenSortieTick` and `_finishRunWithPurpose` reuses it, so the
  income is banked exactly once. The test asserts the reuse rather than adding a
  guard in the tick.
- **C4 — a fully held ring raises no attack.** `runFrontierTick` reports no
  attacks on a secured ring (no unheld neighbour to launch from), which is
  exactly the fully-held fixture the income tests need for the `180` check.

### AC coverage

AC1–AC8 are all delivered by this single item; the AC coverage review reports
full coverage (`proceed`) because the item has no children and is not split.

### Estimate

The `effort_and_risk_skill` estimate recorded on this item (Small effort,
Medium risk, expected 5.33 h, recommended 12.83 h) already reflects this scope
and planning adds no children to re-aggregate, so it is retained unchanged
rather than re-posted.

### Open questions

None — Q1–Q3 were answered by the producer on 2026-11-17 (see the Appendix).
The `10 × aggression` rate being far above the ~24-minerals-per-deployment
anchor stays a documented balance note (see Constraints) with any retune as a
separate follow-up, per the producer's Q1 choice.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-18 — plan skill session: reviewed the intake brief against the code
  (`runFrontierTick`, `applyDefence`, `buildDefenceReport`,
  `PlayScene._resolveBetweenSortieTick`/`_saveHangarWarPayload`, `hexIntel`
  overlay); confirmed no children are warranted; added the Plan section,
  clarifications C1–C4, two missing key files and the test-first ordering;
  retained the existing effort/risk estimate; advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions

Answers recorded from the producer (2026-11-17, interactive reply on
AH-0MWL8CDGN005878A).

- **Q1 — Income formula and rate.** How many minerals should each held hex
  produce per tick?
  - (a) Flat `1` per held hex per tick — full ring 1 pays `6`/tick, full ring 2
    pays `12`/tick.
  - (b) Ring-scaled `heldHexCount × ringIndex` — full ring 1 pays `6`/tick,
    full ring 2 pays `24`/tick.
  - (c) A flat `5`/tick whenever at least one hex is held, regardless of count.
  - **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (producer):** `10 × hex aggression` — each held hex pays
    `10 × that hex's aggression`, summed over held hexes. Source: interactive
    reply to this intake session. This supersedes all three drafted options and
    is captured as AC1 and
    `HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION = 10`.

- **Q2 — Timing when a hex falls this tick.** Should a hex that is lost to a
  frontier attack during the same tick still pay income for that tick?
  - (a) Count hexes held **at the start** of the tick (before this tick's
    attacks).
  - (b) Count hexes still held **after** the tick.
  - **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (producer):** **(b)** — count hexes still held after the tick, so
    a hex lost this tick pays nothing. Source: interactive reply. Captured as
    AC3.

- **Q3 — Visibility.** Should the between-sortie report/map announce the income?
  - (a) Announce it as `HEX INCOME BANKED: +N MINERALS`, mirroring
    `WIN BONUS BANKED`.
  - (b) Bank silently, with no new UI line.
  - **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (producer):** **(a)** — announce the income line. Source:
    interactive reply. Captured as AC4.

### Research notes

- Searched `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D), the GDD §8.2 economy
  notes, `README.md` and the changelog: the design names a "per-tick arithmetic
  rule over the region's holdings" but fixes no rate, hence the Q1 question.
- Searched the worklog (`wl search minerals`, `wl search "owned hex"`,
  `wl search "salvage income"`): no existing or completed item delivers
  per-tick held-hex income; the closest are the win bonus
  (AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2) and salvage banking (AH-0MVUXC118004B4OX).
- Inspected `runFrontierTick`, `applyDefence`, `PlayScene._resolveBetweenSortieTick`,
  `GymHexWar`, `salvageBanking.ts`, `defenceReport.ts` and
  `hexRingDefinitions.ts`: the tick is already the single per-sortie
  transition, `held`/`aggression` and the balance already exist, and the report
  already has an announcement-line pattern, so the feature is a small, local
  addition. `applyDefence` keeps a fallen hex's aggression, so the post-tick
  rule must gate on `held`, not on aggression.
- Income anchor from AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA: ring-1 grind ~24 minerals mean,
  ring-2 grind ~22.3 mean per deployment. At `10 × aggression` a fully held
  ring 1 pays `180`/tick, which is far above that anchor — flagged as a balance
  note for a possible re-baselining follow-up, not a blocker.

## Summary

Test-first contract for the sectioned Hex Map (child of AH-0MWL4QCVD007WOAM).
Pins the structural contract before the renderer is re-laid-out: the
`HexMapView.sections` registry, section headings, non-overlap and in-frame
bounds, `last-sortie` visibility, and the `selected-hex` intel/attack-row
grouping. Position-only pins may be updated; behaviour pins may not be weakened.

## Acceptance Criteria

- HexMapView publishes a sections list of { key, heading, rect } per rendered section; sections do not overlap and every rect lies inside the 960x540 frame.
- Section registry pins assert the keys, headings, non-overlap and in-frame bounds in HexMapScene.test.ts, the renderer tests and GymHexWar.test.ts.
- Tests pin that the run result line, hangar-assault banner and banked win-bonus line render only inside last-sortie, and that the section is absent when the landing carries none of the three.
- Tests pin that the selected-hex intel and its ATTACK - FOCUSED HEX row share one selected-hex section, and the attack row is hidden when the focused hex is in no attack.
- Regression coverage: HexMapScene.test.ts, the renderer/hexIntel tests and GymHexWar.test.ts pin the section registry (keys, headings, non-overlap, in-frame), last-sortie visibility toggling, and that the selected-hex intel and attack row share a section; position-only pins may be updated, behaviour pins may not be weakened.
- The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Test intent

- **Registry shape:** every rendered text object, tile and arrow resolves to
  exactly one section rect (`{ key, heading, rect }`).
- **Geometry:** no two section rects overlap; every rect is inside the
  960x540 frame.
- **Grouping:** `selected-hex` holds both the intel body and the attack row;
  `last-sortie` appears only when the landing carries a run result, an assault
  or a win bonus.
- **Parity:** `GymHexWar` renders the same section keys and headings through the
  same `renderHexMap` call.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts` - section registry, last-sortie toggle and selected-hex grouping pins; update position-only assertions
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts` - parity pins for the same sections
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` - shared section-heading constant pins

## Impact

The sectioned map's promises — the five regions, their headings, their published geometry and the single home for post-sortie news — are now pinned by tests, so a future layout change that breaks the grouping fails loudly instead of shipping.

# Goal

As a player, after a hex battle I want the ship I flew to be spent — win or loss — so each sortie is a real commitment and a bad run costs me the ship, not my collection.

## Context

The gameplay slice of **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF** (producer Q2 = B: a win leaves the hull as the hex's defender and still spends it; a loss destroys it; the difference is economic — a win pays more salvage). Today both resolvers clone the payload and **preserve** the equipped ship, and the defeat path persists nothing at all.

## Scope

- Thread the flown ship into the pure capture cycle: `resolveHexCapture` and `resolveDeploymentDefeat` take the deployment's `DeployedShip` (hull + active loadout as flown), falling back to the hangar's own resolved `activeHull` / `resolveActiveLoadout` when a caller passes none.
- Apply `consumeDeployedShip` on the **win** path (`resolveHexCapture`) and the **loss** path (`resolveDeploymentDefeat`), after the salvage settlement/banking so consumption can never change a balance, and after `leaveDefender` so the defending bot still derives from the flown hull.
- A `campaignReset` (ring-end hangar falls, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J) still returns the freshly reset campaign — the reset wins over consumption.
- `PlayScene`: pass `this.hangarWarDeployment`'s hull and loadout into both calls, and make the loss path persist the consumed payload through the existing demo-guarded `_saveHangarWarPayload` so ownership, banking and the win bonus land in **one** write per battle. `_forfeitUnbankedSalvage` currently writes nothing.
- Keep the demo/attract guard intact: an attract run must never write the consumed payload over the player's war.
- Gym↔game parity: the headless seam (`GymHexWar.captureHex` and the pure resolvers) exercises the same code; no scene-only rule.
- Update the module doc comments that state "losing a run never loses the hangar" to the new rule (the flown ship is spent; the hangar and ring otherwise persist).

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a winning deployment the payload has the flown hull (unless starter), flown starting weapons (unless starter), flown modifiers and their level rows removed; `activeHull` is the starter hull and `activeLoadout` is empty; the win bonus and the banked salvage still land; exactly one payload write happens.
- After a losing deployment the same consumption happens and the payload is persisted exactly once through the demo-guarded write; only the salvage earned since the last bank is forfeited, and the balances are otherwise unchanged by consumption.
- Owned items the player did not fly, their permanent level rows and the free starter kit survive both paths; the post-battle hangar is deployable with an empty loadout (no soft-lock).
- A ring-end `campaignReset` outcome is byte-identical to today's reset payload (consumption does not apply on top of the reset).
- Demo mode (`demoMode` true) leaves the stored `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload untouched on both paths.
- The acceptance tests for consumption (parent test item) go green, and the resolver suites (`captureCycle.test.ts`) plus `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts` pass.
- `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate are green.

- On completion of a hex deployment — **win or loss** — the deployed ship is removed from the hangar payload: the deployed hull (unless it is the free starter hull), every starting weapon in the hangar's active loadout (unless it is the free starter weapon), every modifier in that loadout, and the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` rows for those consumed ids are deleted; every owned item the player did not deploy, and the free starter kit, remain owned. (Restated from the parent item.)
- After the consumption the hangar is reset to the free starter kit: `activeHull` is the starter hull and `activeLoadout` is empty, so the next deployment uses only the free starter kit until the player re-purchases; the player's `bankedMinerals` and `bankedCores` are unchanged by consumption (the existing win bonus still applies on a win). (Restated from the parent item.)

## Key Files

- src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts — `resolveHexCapture` (win) and `resolveDeploymentDefeat` (loss) apply the reducer; module/rule doc comments updated
- src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts — win/loss consumption, campaignReset and refusal-path coverage
- src/scenes/PlayScene.ts — pass the deployment's ship into both resolvers; persist the loss payload once (`_forfeitUnbankedSalvage`, `_saveHangarWarPayload`)
- src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts — expose the exact flown set (`hullId`, `startingWeapons`, `modifiers`) as the `DeployedShip`
- src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts — parity: the gym capture runs the same consuming resolver
- src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts — end-to-end battle-end ownership assertions

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF
- Depends on: the pure reducer item and the acceptance-tests item
- Unchanged by design: AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J (ring-end hangar-falls reset), AH-0MWHF71UG000LI6W (defender upgrade snapshot)

## Impact

Every hex battle now costs the ship you flew, so sorties feel like commitments and the salvage you earn is visibly what funds the next ship.

# Goal

As a player, I want a purchase to arm the part immediately, so re-fitting a new ship after a lost sortie takes one action per part instead of buy-then-hunt-for-equip.

## Context

The economy slice of **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF** (producer Q1 = C refined: "when an upgrade is purchased it is automatically enabled"). Today `buy()` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) documents and implements "buying only grants ownership — equipping stays the deployment selector's job (A5/A6)". This item deliberately supersedes that rule **for the hangar screen only**, while other callers keep the old behaviour through an explicit option.

## Scope

- Add an explicit `equipOnPurchase` option to `buy(hangar, entry, context, options?)`, default **off** so every existing caller (attract/demo decision, tests, gyms) keeps the documented non-equipping behaviour.
- When on and the purchase succeeds: a hull sets `activeHull`, a starting weapon joins `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, a modifier joins `activeLoadout.modifiers` — each deduplicated. A refused purchase (`owned` / `gated` / `unaffordable`) changes neither ownership, balance nor loadout.
- `purchaseHangarEntry` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) opts in, so every hangar-screen purchase lands owned **and** equipped in the same payload.
- `HangarScene` persists the auto-equipped payload through the same single `saveHangarWarPayload` write it already uses, and the screen model (`buildHangarScreenModel` / `renderHangarScreen`) shows the purchased row as equipped/subscribed (`EQUIPPED` / `ON`) on the next render without a second render pass or a hint.
- Keep the un-equip toggles (`equipHangarHull`, `toggleHangarWeapon`, `toggleHangarModifier`) available after an auto-equip — the player can always put a part back on the bench.
- Update the doc comments that state the A5/A6 "buying never equips" rule so they name the hangar-screen opt-in.
- Tests: pure `buy` with and without the option, all three entry kinds, every refusal path, `purchaseHangarEntry` payload result, and the screen model rendering the equipped state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `buy(..., { equipOnPurchase: true })` equips a purchased hull (`activeHull`), weapon (`activeLoadout.startingWeapons`) and modifier (`activeLoadout.modifiers`), and returns the spent price unchanged from today's behaviour.
- `buy(...)` without the option behaves exactly as today (ownership only) — pinned by a test so the A5/A6 contract cannot silently drift for other callers.
- A refused purchase with `equipOnPurchase: true` leaves ownership, balance and loadout identical to before the call (deep-equal payload).
- `purchaseHangarEntry` equips on success and persists nothing on refusal; the screen model built from the resulting payload renders the row as equipped (`EQUIPPED` / `ON`).
- An auto-equipped part can still be un-equipped through the existing toggle functions, and an empty loadout stays legal.
- `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate are green, and the auto-enable acceptance tests go green.

- A successful hangar purchase **auto-enables** the entry: a hull sets `activeHull`, a starting weapon joins `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, and a modifier joins `activeLoadout.modifiers`; a refused purchase (`owned` / `gated` / `unaffordable`) changes neither ownership nor the loadout; this deliberately supersedes the economy's current "buying never equips" rule for the hangar screen, while other callers can keep the old behaviour through an explicit option. (Restated from the parent item.)

## Key Files

- src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts — `equipOnPurchase` option on `buy`; doc comments naming the supersession
- src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts — option/refusal/kind coverage
- src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts — `purchaseHangarEntry` opts in; model/renderer equipped state
- src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarSlice.integration.test.ts — screen-model evidence of the equipped purchase
- src/scenes/HangarScene.ts — persist the auto-equipped payload in the same write
- src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts — doc comment on the "owning never equips" default that now applies only to callers that do not opt in

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF
- Depends on: the acceptance-tests item
- Supersedes for this screen: the A5/A6 "buying only grants ownership" rule
- Follow-on: AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7 (saved ship configurations re-purchase a known build in one action)

## Impact

Buying a part now arms it, so rebuilding a ship after a lost sortie is a handful of clicks rather than a buy-then-equip hunt.

# Goal

As a producer or contributor, I want the documentation to state the new loop — the flown ship is spent each battle and a purchase arms itself — so the design of record, the parity record and the code comments agree with the shipped behaviour.

## Context

Documentation slice of **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF**, after the consumption and auto-enable features land. Several places currently state the opposite rules ("the hangar and the ring never die with the ship"; "buying only grants ownership — equipping stays the deployment selector's job").

## Scope

- **GDD §8.2** (capture cycle): a deployment spends the flown hull, its equipped starting weapons and modifiers plus their permanent levels on **both** outcomes; the hangar resets to the free starter kit with an empty loadout; the win bonus is what makes a win pay for the next ship.
- **GDD §8.1** (hangar slice): a purchase auto-enables the entry (hull → equipped hull, weapon/modifier → active loadout) and a refused purchase leaves ownership and loadout untouched, while the starter weapon stays owned-but-not-equipped for a fresh save.
- **`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`** — Candidate D pillar/persistence text and the capture-cycle description: the hangar persist, but the ship that flew is spent; the ring-end `campaignReset` is unchanged.
- **`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`** — the `GymHangar` and `GymHexWar` rows: the capture the gym resolves now spends the flown ship, and the hangar row the gym renders shows an auto-enabled purchase.
- **`README.md`** — the hangar and hex-map bullets at lines ~361–362: consumption on battle end, reset-to-starter-kit, auto-enable on purchase.
- **Code doc comments** that state the old rules: `hangarEconomy.buy`, `hangarWarStore`'s "owning a starting weapon never equips it" note (clarified, not contradicted: the starter weapon is still owned at zero loadout), `captureCycle`'s "losing a run never loses the hangar" module text, and the `hangarScreen` purchase doc.
- No new balance numbers; the existing win bonus is described, not retuned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- GDD §8.1 and §8.2 describe consumption on win and loss, the reset-to-starter-kit hangar, and auto-enable on purchase, each naming this work item.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D no longer implies the flown ship survives a battle, and still records that the hangar and ring otherwise persist and that the ring-end reset is unchanged.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`'s Hangar War rows describe the consuming capture and the auto-enabling purchase the gym and the game share.
- `README.md`'s hangar and hex-map bullets match the shipped behaviour.
- No code doc comment still asserts the superseded "buying never equips" rule unqualified, and every updated path keeps its existing style (UK English, no invented numbers).
- Documentation-only change: `npm run build` stays green and no behaviour changes.

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. (Restated verbatim from the parent item — this item is where that criterion is satisfied.)

## Key Files

- docs/Game Design Document.md — §8.1 (hangar slice) and §8.2 (capture cycle)
- docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md — Candidate D persistence, pillar impact and capture-cycle text
- docs/GYM_PARITY.md — `GymHangar` / `GymHexWar` rows
- ./README.md — hangar and hex-map bullets
- src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts — `buy` doc comment
- src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts — module and `resolveDeploymentDefeat` doc comments

# Re-fit the human-style knobs to the calmer competent flight model

## Problem statement

The human-style fit (`src/ai/style/fitting.ts`) maps a recorded player's style
onto the competent bot's knobs, but its knob set and mapping constants predate
the calmer flight model shipped by AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 (wider travel-turn
deadband, tight 0.05 rad aim deadband, turn reversal hysteresis, 30 ms turn
press hold, pass-through collection). Because the fit still models the old
precision-turning governor, its synthetic-human fixed point lands on the wrong
side of the 1-point competence tolerance on 20 of the 32 seed-sweep seeds
(was 14), so the "styled bot is measurably closer without regressing
competence" guarantee has silently weakened.

## Users (example user stories)

- **Producer tuning style matching** — "As a producer, I want the style fit to
  stay competent after the bot's flight feel is deliberately changed, so I do
  not have to hand-re-baseline the evaluation every time the flight model
  improves."
- **Player/promo viewer of the attract demo or teaser** — "As a viewer, I want
  the styled bot to play like the recorded human *and* still fly competently,
  so the demonstration is not undermined by an unfitted governor."
- **Future "play like me" feature owner** — "As the owner of a future style
  feature, I want the fit to model the governor the bot actually flies, so
  adding a flight-model knob does not silently invalidate the fit."

## Acceptance Criteria

- The style fitting is re-run against the current (calmer) flight model and
  the `evaluateStyleMatch` seed sweep returns to at most 16 of 32 regressed
  seeds (the original bound), or the bound is re-justified with the newly
  measured distribution (count and measurement date recorded in both the test
  and the docs).
- The fitted knobs include the aim deadband (`aimAlignmentToleranceRad`): it is
  set by `fitStyle`, appears in `StyleFit.applied`, is clamped to a safe
  envelope, and is co-fitted with the fit's aim-fallibility knobs
  (`humanInput.skill` / `maxAimErrorRad`) so the random aim error can never
  exceed the deadband it is aiming into. Where the fit derives it, the
  derivation is geometrically consistent with the fitted `engagementRange` so
  the calibrated standoff does not reintroduce the standoff deadlock.
- The governor turn knobs introduced by the calmer flight model
  (`alignmentToleranceRad`, `turnHysteresisRad`, `turnPressMinMs`) are fitted
  from the existing cadence/hold features, or explicitly documented as
  deliberately left at the shipped defaults, so the fit models the same
  governor the bot flies.
- `docs/STYLE_MATCHING.md` and `docs/EVALUATION.md` record the new fitted
  values and the measurement date: the parameter-fitting table, the
  seed-sweep stability wording and the `src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts`
  comment all state the measured closer/regressed counts, the bound and the
  date; the `styleDocs.test.ts` / `evaluationDocs.test.ts` guards still pass.
- Fitting unit tests cover the new knobs: each is applied and recorded in
  `applied`, clamped at both envelope ends, and `enforceSafety` invariants
  (priority order, survival gap) still hold.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (typecheck, build and
  tests via the test skill).

## Impact

Producers and future style-matching work can trust that fitting a human's style
still yields a competent bot after the flight model was deliberately calmed,
and the sweep's regression bound again means what it says instead of being
widened to accommodate an unfitted governor.

## Constraints

- **Baseline dependency (RESOLVED — landed):** the calmer flight model is
  commit c2e3dadd on `origin/dev` and AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 is `completed`
  (stage `in_review`); the `depends-on` edge to it is still recorded. A stale
  local `dev` (df5d3d3c at plan time) does **not** contain it, so the
  implementer must confirm `aimAlignmentToleranceRad` / `turnHysteresisRad` /
  `turnPressMinMs` are present in their worktree before measuring any sweep —
  `implement.py start` fast-forwards local `dev` to `origin/dev`, which is the
  correct baseline. Measuring against a pre-c2e3dadd tree re-fits the wrong
  governor.
- **Safety invariants unchanged:** `enforceSafety` keeps the fixed priority
  order, band separation and the survival-band margin, and the steering
  safety filter (the never-suicide guarantee) is untouched.
- **Purity and determinism:** fitting stays pure (no wall clock, no I/O); the
  same recording and seed always produce a byte-identical `StyleMatchReport`.
- **Bound policy:** prefer restoring the original ≤16/32 bound. If the
  measured distribution genuinely shifted because the fit legitimately
  changes flight feel, re-justify the bound with the measured distribution
  and date rather than silently widening it, and keep the majority-closer
  assertion.
- **No scope creep:** do not change flight behaviour or the governor's shipped
  defaults in this item (that belongs to AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2); the change
  surface is the fit's knob set/constants, its tests and its docs. New
  opportunities go to linked work items, not into this one.

## Existing state

- `src/ai/style/fitting.ts` fits reaction time, thrust-press durations,
  commitment hysteresis, engagement range, prediction horizon, risk knobs and
  the priority-band tilt. It builds `humanInput` from
  `BOT_HUMAN_INPUT_TUNABLES`, so `alignmentToleranceRad` (0.16),
  `aimAlignmentToleranceRad` (0.05), `turnHysteresisRad` (0.25),
  `turnPressMinMs` (30) and `skill` (1) stay at their shipped defaults and
  never appear in `StyleFit.applied`.
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` (calmer flight model) computes the effective aim
  deadband as `min(alignmentToleranceRad, aimAlignmentToleranceRad)`; aim
  intents are exempt from the turn hysteresis and the press hold.
- `src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts`'s synthetic human iterates `fitStyle` 8×
  over `createCompetentBotBrain`; the calmer-model branch records 20/32
  regressed and pins `regressedCount <= 20`.
- `docs/STYLE_MATCHING.md` ("Parameter fitting" table, "Seed-sweep stability"
  section) and `docs/EVALUATION.md` still describe the old knob set and the
  "must not regress competence on more than half" rule, with no measurement
  date.
- The shipped competent bot itself is unchanged by this item: the fit only
  moves knobs for a caller who applies a style.

## Desired change

Extend `fitStyle` to fit the governor's turn/aim knobs (at minimum
`aimAlignmentToleranceRad`, plus `alignmentToleranceRad`,
`turnHysteresisRad`, `turnPressMinMs`), co-fit aim fallibility with the aim
deadband, re-run the 32-seed sweep on the calmer model, and update
`docs/STYLE_MATCHING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md` and the evaluation test comment
with the new fitted values, measured distribution and date. Restore the
≤16/32 bound if achievable; otherwise re-justify it with evidence.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/style/fitting.ts` — add the governor turn/aim knobs to the fitted
  set, new clamp envelopes, `applied` entries and the aim-skill/deadband
  co-fit.
- `src/ai/style/fitting.test.ts` — assert the new knobs are applied, clamped,
  and that the safety invariants still hold.
- `src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts` — re-measure the 32-seed sweep;
  restore/re-justify the regression bound and record the measurement date.
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — read-only reference for the governor knob
  semantics and defaults (no behaviour change expected).
- `docs/STYLE_MATCHING.md` — parameter-fitting table, seed-sweep stability
  section, measured values and date.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — align the style-sweep regression wording with the
  re-justified bound.
- `src/ai/style/styleDocs.test.ts` — keep the docs guard green (extend it if it
  should assert the new knobs/date).
- `src/ai/eval/evaluationDocs.test.ts` — the EVALUATION.md docs guard; no
  change expected, must stay green (AC4).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** the calmer flight model may not land exactly as the branch
  currently stands (it is awaiting producer re-review), which moves the
  distribution again. **Mitigation:** re-measure after the model lands; record
  the date and counts, and prefer the distribution-stable majority rule over a
  brittle per-seed expectation.
- **Risk:** over-widening the aim deadband hides a real competence loss.
  **Mitigation:** clamp it to a safe envelope tied to the fitted standoff and
  keep the aim-perturbation/deadband invariant tested.
- **Risk:** re-fitting to reduce regressions could be mistaken for re-baselining
  test expectations. **Mitigation:** ACs require either the original bound or
  an evidence-backed re-justification, not a silent widening.
- **Scope-creep risk:** new flight-model knobs appearing mid-work. **Mitigation:**
  record them as linked follow-up work; this item covers the knobs the calmer
  model already introduced.
- **Assumption:** the fit can derive an aim deadband from the existing
  `StyleFeatures` (engagement distance and risk) without adding a new
  human-recording feature; if a dedicated aim-precision feature proves
  necessary, that is a linked follow-up, not scope here.
- **Assumption:** "the fit's aim skill" is the governor's existing
  `humanInput.skill` / `maxAimErrorRad` pair; the fit need not start fitting
  `skill` from a feature, but it must enforce the deadband/error invariant.

## Related work

- AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 — "Bot oscillates too much" (in progress): the calmer
  competent flight model this item re-fits against; the source of the 20/32
  regression.
- AH-0MUY08XXN003NV0I — "Style matching from telemetry" (completed): delivered
  `fitStyle`, `evaluateStyleMatch` and `docs/STYLE_MATCHING.md`.
- AH-0MV03PVZI009870X — "Make bot micro-simulation tests robust to small feel
  tweaks" (completed): the distribution-stable sweep precedent this bound
  follows.
- AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A — "Bot is more gentle on the thrusters" (completed):
  prior feel tweak that forced a style re-seed.
- AH-0MVT2W3RS009ZB2X — "Retire the wallMargin tunable" (completed): prior
  fitting-surface change and its docs/test updates.
- AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98 — "Bot rotation skills" (completed): aim
  skill/fallibility knob the aim-deadband co-fit interacts with.
- Repository docs: `docs/STYLE_MATCHING.md` (fitting + evaluation contract),
  `docs/EVALUATION.md` (sweep assertions), `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` (competent
  brain and governor).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which flight-model baseline should the re-fit be measured against?" —
  Answer (agent, from repo evidence): the calmer model on branch
  `wl-AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2-bot-oscillates-too-much` (commit c2e3dadd).
  AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 is in progress and awaiting producer re-review, so this
  item is recorded as `Blocked-by: AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2` until the model lands
  on `dev`. Source: `git log --all`, `git worktree list`, parent audit result.
  **Recommended:** measure only once the calmer model is the baseline — a fit
  measured against `dev` re-fits the wrong governor.
- Q: "Restore the original ≤16/32 bound, or re-justify the bound?" — Answer
  (agent, from the item's own AC): prefer restoring ≤16/32; re-justify only if
  the measured distribution shows the shift is legitimate, recording the count
  and date in the test and docs. Source: this work item's acceptance criteria.
  **Recommended:** restore the original bound.
- Q: "How should the aim deadband be fitted, given there is no dedicated
  aim-precision feature?" — Answer (agent assumption, to be validated by the
  implementer): derive `aimAlignmentToleranceRad` from the fitted
  `engagementRange` and the governor's aim-fallibility knobs so the fit stays
  geometrically hittable at its fitted standoff, clamped to a safe envelope;
  no new human feature. Source: `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` aim-deadband `min()`
  semantics and `src/ai/style/fitting.ts` clamps. **Recommended:** derive from
  the fitted standoff and co-fit with `maxAimErrorRad`, not a new feature.
- Q: "Should the new travel-turn knobs also be fitted?" — Answer (agent
  assumption): yes, fit `alignmentToleranceRad`, `turnHysteresisRad` and
  `turnPressMinMs` from the cadence/hold features (or document why they stay
  at defaults), because they are the human-style knobs the title names and the
  fit must model the governor the bot flies. Source: the calmer-model branch's
  `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` knob set. **Recommended:** fit them.
- Duplicate-work check: performed — `wl search` over "style fitting aim
  deadband", "style match evaluation regression" and "regressed seeds style"
  found no completed or open item that already satisfies these acceptance
  criteria. No duplicate.
